zajjaj:81-81.t: ﴿وَكَيْفَ أخافُ ما أشْرَكْتُمْ ولا تَخافُونَ أنَّكم أشْرَكْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ ما لَمْ يُنَـزِّلْ بِهِ عَلَيْكم سُلْطانًا﴾, that is: and you yourselves do not fear your associating with Allah that for which He has sent down to you no authority (سُلْطان), i.e. no clear proof. ﴿فَأيُّ الفَرِيقَيْنِ أحَقُّ بِالأمْنِ﴾, that is: which has more right to be safe from the punishment — the one who affirms the oneness of Allah, or the one who associates partners with Him?

zajjaj:82-82.t: And His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ولَمْ يَلْبِسُوا إيمانَهم بِظُلْمٍ أُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ الأمْنُ﴾: they said it is possible that this — ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ الأمْنُ﴾ — is the speech of Allah, not a report of what Ibrāhīm said; and it is possible that Ibrāhīm said it.

zajjaj:84-84.t: And His saying: ﴿وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِ داوُدَ وسُلَيْمانَ﴾: ”داوُدَ وسُلَيْمانَ“ are conjoined (nasaq, i.e. maʿṭūf — conjoined) to ”نُوحًا“, as though He said: "and We guided Dāwūd and Sulaymān". It is possible that it means "of the offspring of Nūḥ" (”مِن ذُرِّيَّةِ نُوحٍ“), and it is possible that it means "of the offspring of Ibrāhīm" (”مِن ذُرِّيَّةِ إبْراهِيمَ“), because both of them have already been mentioned. The names of the prophets that come after His saying ﴿وَنُوحًا هَدَيْنا مِن قَبْلُ﴾ are conjoined to ”نُوحًا“, except that of ”اَلْيَسَعَ“ one says both ”اَللَّيْسَعَ“ and ”اَلْيَسَعَ“, with the lām doubled and undoubled.

zajjaj:87-87.t: And His saying: ﴿وَمِن آبائِهِمْ وذُرِّيّاتِهِمْ وإخْوانِهِمْ﴾, that is: We guided these, and We guided some of their fathers and their brothers. The meaning of His saying ﴿واجْتَبَيْناهُمْ﴾ is like "We chose them" (”اِخْتَرْناهم“). It is taken from ”جَبَيْتُ الماءَ في الحَوْضِ“ ("I gathered the water in the basin"), said when you collect it.

zajjaj:89-89.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَإنْ يَكْفُرْ بِها هَؤُلاءِ﴾, that is: those to whom you have been sent who have disbelieved and do disbelieve. ﴿فَقَدْ وكَّلْنا بِها قَوْمًا لَيْسُوا بِها بِكافِرِينَ﴾, that is: We have entrusted [a people] with believing in them. Three views have been given about this. It is said that He means by it the prophets who have been mentioned, who believed, at the time they were sent, in what the Prophet ﷺ brought. It is said that He means by it the angels. And it is also said that He means by it those of the Companions of the Prophet and his followers who believed. And — Allah knows best — He means by it the earlier prophets, because of His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ هَدى اللَّهُ فَبِهُداهُمُ اقْتَدِهِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 90], that is: the prophets whom We have mentioned are those whom Allah guided; ﴿فَبِهُداهُمُ اقْتَدِهِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 90], that is: be patient as they were patient, for their peoples denied them and they bore patiently being denied and being harmed, so follow their example.

This hāʾ in ”اِقْتَدِهْ“ is retained only in pause (waqf); by it the kasra of the dāl is made clear. If you join (waṣl), you say ”اِقْتَدِ“. ﴿قُلْ لا أسْألُكُمْ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 90]. Abū Isḥāq [i.e. al-Zajjāj] said: What those whose knowledge I trust have chosen is that one should pause at this hāʾ; and likewise in His saying ﴿فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ اقْرَءُوا كِتابِيَهْ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 19] ﴿إنِّي ظَنَنْتُ أنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 20], and likewise ﴿لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 259], and likewise ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 10]. We have already explained what there is in ”يَتَسَنَّهْ“ in Sūrat al-Baqara.

zajjaj:91-91.t: And His saying: ﴿وَما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ إذْ قالُوا ما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلى بَشَرٍ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾: its meaning is: they did not magnify Allah with the magnification due to Him, when they denied His revelation. That is because a group of the Jews — of their hypocrites — came, opposing the Prophet ﷺ obstinately, disputing with him and turning people away from him. Their appearance was the appearance of the rabbis (al-aḥbār); they lived in luxury and did not devote themselves to worship. So the Prophet ﷺ informed them that it is in the Torah that Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, does not love the fat rabbi. So they denied the Torah and said: "Allah has not sent down anything to any human being." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ مَن أنْـزَلَ الكِتابَ الَّذِي جاءَ بِهِ مُوسى نُورًا وهُدًى لِلنّاسِ تَجْعَلُونَهُ قَراطِيسَ تُبْدُونَها وتُخْفُونَ كَثِيرًا﴾: they show what they like of it and hide much. ﴿وَعُلِّمْتُمْ ما لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا﴾, that is: you have been taught, on the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ, what neither you nor your fathers knew. ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ ذَرْهم في خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾: of anyone engaged in work that brings no benefit it is said: ”إنَّما أنْتَ لاعِبٌ“ ("you are only playing").

zajjaj:92-92.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلِتُنْذِرَ أُمَّ القُرى ومَن حَوْلَها﴾: ”لِتُنْذِرَ“ is read both with tāʾ and with yāʾ. The meaning is: We sent it down for blessing and for warning. The meaning of ”أُمَّ القُرى“ is: the people of Umm al-Qurā (the Mother of Towns); ”وَمَن حَوْلَها“ is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to them. Umm al-Qurā is Makka; it was called Umm al-Qurā because it was the greatest of the towns in standing.

zajjaj:93-93.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَمَن أظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا أوْ قالَ أُوحِيَ إلَيَّ ولَمْ يُوحَ إلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that He means by it Musaylima and the man of Ṣanʿāʾ, because the two of them claimed prophethood.

﴿وَمَن قالَ سَأُنْـزِلُ مِثْلَ ما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾: the position of ”مَن“ is genitive (jarr). The meaning is: "And who does greater wrong than the one who invents [a lie], and the one who says: I will send down the like of what Allah has sent down" (”وَمَن أظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى ومَن قالَ سَأُنْزِلُ مِثْلَ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ“). This is an answer to their saying: ﴿لَوْ نَشاءُ لَقُلْنا مِثْلَ هَذا﴾ [al-Anfāl: 31].

And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرى إذِ الظّالِمُونَ في غَمَراتِ المَوْتِ﴾: the answer (jawāb) of ”لَوْ“ is omitted. The meaning is: "If you were to see when the wrongdoers are in the floods of death, you would see a mighty punishment." Of anyone who is in a great deal of something it is said: ”قَدْ غَمَرَ فُلانًا ذَلِكَ“ ("that has flooded so-and-so"), and it is said: ”قَدْ غَمَرَ فُلانًا الدَّيْنُ“ ("debt has flooded so-and-so"). Its interpretation is: it has become so much that, in what is known, it is like what is seen to have been flooded and covered over by its abundance.

And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والمَلائِكَةُ باسِطُو أيْدِيهِمْ﴾, that is: [stretching them] against them with punishment. As for the meaning of ﴿أخْرِجُوا أنْفُسَكُمُ﴾, there are two aspects in it — and Allah knows best: "they say: Bring out your souls." It is possible that it is as you say to someone you are tormenting: ”لَأُزْهِقَنَّ نَفْسَكَ“ ("I will surely make your soul depart") and ”لَأُخْرِجَنَّ نَفْسَكَ“ ("I will surely bring out your soul"); so they say — and Allah knows best — "bring out your souls" in this sense. And it is possible that the meaning is: "free your souls" (”خَلِّصُوا أنْفُسَكم“), that is: you are not able to escape. ﴿اليَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الهُونِ﴾, that is: the punishment by which the severe punishment befalls.

zajjaj:94-94.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونا فُرادى كَما خَلَقْناكم أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾: as for the meaning of ”فُرادى“, it is "each one alone, separated from his partner in error and from his full brother". As for the meaning of ﴿كَما خَلَقْناكم أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾, it has come in the exegesis: naked and uncircumcised (ghurl); ”اَلْغُرْلُ“ are the uncircumcised (al-ghulf). What the language also allows is: "as We began you the first time", that is: your resurrection is like your creation.

And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾: the nominative (rafʿ) is better, and its meaning is: your bond has been cut. The accusative (naṣb) is permissible; the meaning is: what you had of partnership between you has been cut off.

zajjaj:95-95.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ فالِقُ الحَبِّ والنَّوى﴾, that is: He splits the dry, dead grain and the dry date-stone, and brings out of them green leaves. That is the meaning of ﴿يُخْرِجُ الحَيَّ مِنَ المَيِّتِ﴾, that is: He brings out the tender, fresh, green plant from the dry grain. ﴿وَمُخْرِجُ المَيِّتِ مِنَ الحَيِّ﴾: and He brings out the dry grain from the living, growing plant. Allah, exalted is His praise, argued against them by what they witness of His creation, because they denied the resurrection; so He informed them that He is the One who created these things, and that He is able to raise them.

And His saying: ﴿فَأنّى تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾, that is: so from where are you turned away from the truth?

zajjaj:96-96.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فالِقُ الإصْباحِ﴾: the meaning of ”اَلْإصْباحُ“ and ”اَلصُّبْحُ“ (daybreak) is one. It is possible that it is "the Creator of daybreak", and it is possible that its meaning is "the One who splits the dawn" (”شاقُّ الصُّبْحِ“), and that goes back to the meaning of "the Creator of the dawn" (”خالِقُ الصُّبْحِ“).

And His saying: ﴿والشَّمْسَ والقَمَرَ حُسْبانًا﴾: the accusative (naṣb) in ”اَلشَّمْسَ والقَمَرَ“ is the reading, and the genitive (jarr) is permissible, in the sense of "and the One who makes the sun and the moon a reckoning" (”وَجاعِلُ الشَّمْسِ والقَمَرِ حُسْبانًا“), because in ”جاعِلُ“ there is the meaning of ”جَعَلَ“ (He made), and by it ”سَكَنًا“ is put in the accusative. It is not permissible to say ”جاعِلُ اللَّيْلَ سَكَنًا“, because active participles (asmāʾ al-fāʿilīn), when the verb has been raised «[Translator's note: so in the text — "قَدْ رُفِعَ"; the sense required is "when the action is already past" (perhaps a corruption of "قد مضى" or "وقع")]», are annexed to what follows them and nothing else. You say ”هَذا ضارِبُ زَيْدٍ أمْسِ“ ("this is the one who struck Zayd yesterday"), and the consensus of the grammarians is that the accusative is not permissible in Zayd; most of the Kufans hold this, though some of the Kufans permit the accusative. So if you say ”هَذا مُعْطِي زَيْدٍ دِرْهَمًا“ ("this is the one who gave Zayd a dirham"), the accusative of the dirham is carried on [an implied] ”أعْطى“ (gave).

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Anʿām
﷽
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: It has reached me from a source I trust that Sūrat "al-Anʿām" was revealed all of it at once, brought down by seventy thousand angels raising a loud chorus (zajal) of glorification, and that most of it is argumentation against the polytheists of the Arabs, against those who denied the resurrection and the raising of the dead. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, began with His own praise, saying: ﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ﴾. He mentioned the greatest of created things, because the sky is without pillars that you see, and the earth does not sway with us. Then He mentioned the darkness and the light, and He mentioned the matter of the night and the day, which are among the things by which creation is sustained. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that these are His creation, and that their Creator has nothing like Him; and He made known along with that that those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord (يَعْدِلُونَ), i.e. they set up an equal (ʿadīl) to Allah, and so worship lifeless stones, while they acknowledge that Allah is the Creator of what He has described.

zajjaj:2-2.t: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known to them that He created them from clay, and He mentioned in another place the states of created beings as sperm-drops, clinging clots, and lumps of flesh, formed and unformed. That is because the polytheists doubted the resurrection and said: ﴿مَن يُحْيِي العِظامَ وهي رَمِيمٌ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 78]. So He, Mighty and Majestic, made known to them that the One who brought them into being, and brought the bones into being, and created these things — not from any thing — is able to create their like, and He will bring them to life after their death. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكم مِن طِينٍ ثُمَّ قَضى أجَلا﴾, i.e. He appointed a term for your lives, i.e. a time during which you live; ﴿وَأجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ﴾, meaning the matter of the Hour and the resurrection; ﴿ثُمَّ أنْتُمْ﴾ after this clear exposition ﴿تَمْتَرُونَ﴾, i.e. you doubt.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَهُوَ اللَّهُ في السَّماواتِ وفي الأرْضِ﴾: «في» is connected in meaning with what the name "Allah" indicates. The meaning is: He is the Creator, the Knower of that by which the affair of the heaven and the earth is set right; the meaning is: He is the One alone in governing [all things] in the heavens and the earth. If you said «هو زيدٌ في البيت والدار» ("he is Zayd in the house and the dwelling"), it would not be permissible, unless there were in the speech an indication that Zayd manages the affairs of the house and the dwelling, so that the meaning would be: he is the manager in the dwelling and the house. And if you said «هو المعتضدُ الخليفةُ في الشرق والغرب» ("he is al-Muʿtaḍid, the caliph, in the East and the West"), or «هو المعتضدُ في الشرق والغرب», it would be permissible on this basis. It may also be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, as if it were said: "He is Allah, and He is in the heavens and in the earth". Similar to the first view is: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي في السَّماءِ إلَهٌ وفي الأرْضِ إلَهٌ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84]. It may also be that «وهو الله في السماوات وفي الأرض» means: He is the One worshipped in both of them; and this is close to the first view.

His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِيهِمْ أنْباءُ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 5]: by this He indicated that they used to mock, and their mockery has been mentioned elsewhere. The meaning of its "coming" is: its outcome (taʾwīl); the meaning is: they will come to know what their mockery leads to.

His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ألَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أهْلَكْنا مِن قَبْلِهِمْ مِن قَرْنٍ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 6]: the position of «كم» is accusative by «أهلكنا», except that what precedes this interrogative does not govern it. It has been said that "al-qarn" is eighty years, and it has been said seventy. What appears to me — and Allah knows best — is that "al-qarn" is the people of a period in which there was a prophet, or in which there was a generation (ṭabaqa) of people of knowledge, whether the years were few or many. The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «خيركم قرني» ("the best of you are my generation"), i.e. my Companions — Allah's mercy be upon them — "then those who follow them", meaning the Followers (al-tābiʿūn), "then those who follow them", meaning those who took [knowledge] from the Followers. It is also possible that "al-qarn" refers to the whole community (umma), and these are generations (qurūn) within it. The derivation of «القرن» is from «الاقتران» (being joined together); so its interpretation is that the qarn are those who were joined together in that time, and those who come after them are of another joining.

His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَأرْسَلْنا السَّماءَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِدْرارًا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 6], i.e. possessing abundant rain. The pattern «مِفْعال» is among the nouns of intensiveness (asmāʾ al-mubālagha). One says «ديمة مدرار» (a persistent downpour) when its rain is abundant and continuous. This is like their saying «امرأة مذكار», when a woman gives birth to many males, and likewise «مئناث» for females.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَوْ نَـزَّلْنا عَلَيْكَ كِتابًا في قِرْطاسٍ فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأيْدِيهِمْ لَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إنْ هَذا إلا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that they had become rooted (aṣilū) in evil falsehood in rejecting prophethood, for they had seen the moon split, yet turned away and said: "continuous magic". Likewise they say of everything that created beings are incapable of: "magic". This is the very essence of rejecting the utmost truth and the radiant, clear light. Had they seen the Book coming down from the sky, they would have said "magic", just as they said of the splitting of the moon: "magic".
[Translator's note: «أصِلُوا» is as printed; the sense appears to be "persisted / became rooted".]

zajjaj:8-8.t:
﴿وَقالُوا لَوْلا أُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ﴾: they mean upon the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿وَلَوْ أنْـزَلْنا مَلَكًا لَقُضِيَ الأمْرُ ثُمَّ لا يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ means — and Allah knows best — that signs are among the things with which no respite takes place. The meaning of «لقضي الأمر» is: it would have been completed by destroying them.

«قُضِيَ» in the language has several senses, all of which go back to the meaning of the cutting off of a thing and its completion. Among them is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿ثُمَّ قَضى أجَلا وأجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 2], meaning: then He decreed after that and completed it. Among them is command, which is His words: ﴿وَقَضى رَبُّكَ ألا تَعْبُدُوا إلا إيّاهُ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 23], meaning: He commanded, except that it is a decisive, binding command. Among them is informing.

And His words: ﴿وَقَضَيْنا إلى بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ في الكِتابِ لَتُفْسِدُنَّ في الأرْضِ مَرَّتَيْنِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 4], i.e. We informed them decisively. Among them is judgement (al-qaḍāʾ), the decisive separation in a ruling, which is His words: ﴿وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَبِّكَ إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 14]. Like that is your saying «قد قضى القاضي بين الخصوم» ("the judge has judged between the litigants"), i.e. he has decided between them in the ruling. Of that also is «قد قضى فلان دينه» ("so-and-so has settled his debt"), whose interpretation is: he cut off what his creditor had against him, paid it to him, and cut off what was between him and him. Everything that is made firm has been «قُضِي»; you say «قد قضيت هذا الثوب» and «قد قضيت هذه الدار» when you have made it and made its making firm. Abū Dhuʾayb al-Hudhalī said:
؎وَعَلَيْهِما مَسْرُودَتانِ قَضاهُما ∗∗∗ داوُدُ أوْ صَنَعَ السَّوابِغَ تُبَّعُ
(Upon the two of them were two coats of linked mail which Dāwūd had wrought (qaḍāhumā), or Tubbaʿ, maker of full-length mail.)

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ مَلَكًا لَجَعَلْناهُ رَجُلا﴾, i.e. had We sent an angel to them, We would only have sent him in the form of a human being, because — as has been said — if anyone looked at an angel in its own form, he would be struck down senseless. The angels used to come to the prophets in human form. Of that is that Jibrīl used to come to the Prophet, upon him be peace, when he descended with revelation, in the form of Diḥya al-Kalbī. Of it also is the story of the disputants when they climbed over the wall of the sanctuary (miḥrāb), for they came to Dāwūd as two angels in the form of two men bringing their dispute to him. Of it also is that the angels came to Ibrāhīm in the form of guests, and likewise they came to Lūṭ. For that reason it was said: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ مَلَكًا لَجَعَلْناهُ رَجُلا﴾.

And His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَلَبَسْنا عَلَيْهِمْ ما يَلْبِسُونَ﴾: one says «لبَستُ الأمرَ على القوم ألبِسُه» when you have made the matter obscure to them and made it confusing to them. They used to confuse their weaker folk regarding the matter of the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "This is only a human being like you". So He said [in effect]: "Had We sent down an angel and they saw the angel as a man, the same confusion would have befallen them regarding him as befell their weaker folk on their account".

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His words: ﴿فَحاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنهم ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾: "al-ḥayq" in the language is the harm that envelops a person because of something he did. Of it is His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلا يَحِيقُ المَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إلا بِأهْلِهِ﴾ [Fāṭir: 43], i.e. the consequence of its harm returns only upon them.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَتَبَ عَلى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ لَيَجْمَعَنَّكم إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed His favour upon His servants by granting them respite despite their disbelief and their venturing upon the major sins He had forbidden them — by deferring them, giving them long life and giving them room so that they might repent. That is His prescribing mercy for Himself. As for ﴿لَيَجْمَعَنَّكم إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾, it is an argument against the polytheists who rejected the resurrection; so He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿لَيَجْمَعَنَّكم إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾, i.e. to the day which you have denied, just as you say «قد جمعت هؤلاء إلى هؤلاء» ("I have gathered these to those"), i.e. I have brought them together in one gathering.

And His words: ﴿الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾: al-Akhfash mentioned that «الذين» is a badal (substitute) for the kāf and the mīm [of «ليجمعنكم»], the meaning being: He will surely gather these polytheists, who have lost their own selves, to this day which they deny and disbelieve in. What I hold is that His words ﴿الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ are in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is ﴿فَهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, because «ليجمعنكم» encompasses all of creation — those who have lost their own selves and others.

This lām in «ليجمعنكم» is the lām of the oath (lām al-qasam). So it is possible that the speech is complete at «كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة», and then He began anew, saying «ليجمعنكم», as if the meaning were: "By Allah, He will surely gather you". It is also possible that «ليجمعنكم» is a badal (substitute) for «الرحمة», explaining it, because when He said ﴿كَتَبَ رَبُّكم عَلى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 54], He explained His mercy as His granting them respite until the Day of Resurrection, and in the respite there is what we explained just above.
[Translator's note: the author quotes the phrase here in the wording of al-Anʿām 54 («كتب ربكم»); the ayah under discussion (al-Anʿām 12) reads «كَتَبَ عَلى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ».]

zajjaj:98-98.t: And His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أنْشَأكم مِن نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ ومُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾: most readers read ”مُسْتَقَرٌّ“ with fatḥa on the qāf, and it has also been read with kasra on it; ”مُسْتَوْدَعٌ“ is with fatḥa only. As for the nominative (rafʿ) of ”مُسْتَقَرٌّ ومُسْتَوْدَعٌ“, it is in the sense of "you have a place of settling and you have a place of deposit" (”لَكم مُسْتَقَرٌّ ولَكم مُسْتَوْدَعٌ“). Whoever reads it with kasra, ”فَمُسْتَقِرٌّ ومُسْتَوْدَعٌ“, reads it in the sense of "so of you there is one settled and of you there is one deposited" (”فَمِنكم مُسْتَقِرٌّ ومِنكم مُسْتَوْدَعٌ“). The interpretation of ”مُسْتَقِرٌّ“ is: settled in the womb; ”وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ“, that is: of you there is one deposited in the loins of men. On this too is ”فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ“ with fatḥa on the qāf, ”وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ“, that is: "so they have a place of settling, and you have in the loins a place of deposit" (”فَلَهم مُسْتَقَرٌّ ولَكم في الأصْلابِ مُسْتَوْدَعٌ“). It is possible that ”فَمُسْتَقِرٌّ“ with kasra, ”وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ“, means: "so of you there is one settled among the living, and of you there is one deposited", that is: one settled in this world, existing, and one deposited in the loins, not yet created. And it is possible that ”فَمُسْتَقِرٌّ“ with kasra, ”وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ“, means: "so of you there is one settled among the living, and of you there is one deposited in the soil". All these views have been stated, and Allah knows best the truth of that.

zajjaj:99-99.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أنْـزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً﴾: the lexicographers said: the origin of the word ”ماءٌ“ (water) is ”ماهٌ“, except that the hamza was substituted for the hāʾ because of the faintness of the hāʾ. The proof of that is their saying ”أمْواهٌ“ in its plural, and ”مِياهٌ“, and it is made diminutive as ”مُوَيْهٌ“. The poet said:
؎سَقى اللَّهُ أمْواهًا عَرَفْتُ مَكانَها ∗∗∗ جُرابًا ومَلْكُومًا وبَذَّرَ والغَمْرَ
(May Allah water waters whose places I have known: Jurāb, Malkūm, Badhdhar and al-Ghamr.)

And His saying: ﴿فَأخْرَجْنا مِنهُ خَضِرًا﴾: the meaning of ”خَضِرٌ“ is like the meaning of ”أخْضَرُ“ (green). One says ”اِخْضَرَّ، فَهو أخْضَرُ، وخَضِرٌ“ ("it became green, so it is akhḍar and khaḍir"), like ”اِعْوَرَّ، فَهو أعْوَرُ، وعَوِرٌ“ ("he became one-eyed, so he is aʿwar and ʿawir").

And His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّخْلِ مِن طَلْعِها قِنْوانٌ دانِيَةٌ﴾: ”قِنْوانٌ“ is the plural of ”قِنْوٌ“, like ”صِنْوٌ“ and ”صِنْوانٌ“. When you make qinw dual, the two are ”قِنْوانِ يا هَذا“ ("two qinws, O you"), with kasra on the nūn. ”اَلْقِنْوُ“ is the ʿidhq, with kasra on the ʿayn, which is the date-cluster (al-kibāsa); and ”اَلْعَذْقُ“ [with fatḥa] is the palm tree. ﴿دانِيَةٌ﴾, that is: near to reach. He did not say "and of them are distant clusters", because there is in the speech an indication that the distant, far-off [cluster] of the palm was once not far off, and mention of the near was deemed sufficient in place of mention of the distant, just as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 81], and did not say "and garments that protect you from the cold", because there is in the speech an indication that they protect from the cold, since what shields from heat shields from cold.

And His saying: ﴿وَجَنّاتٍ مِن أعْنابٍ﴾ is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to His saying ”خَضِرًا“, that is: "So We brought forth from the water green growth, and gardens of grapes." ”اَلْجَنَّةُ“ is the orchard (al-bustān). The orchard is called ”جَنَّةً“ — and every dense growth, part of which covers other parts, is a ”جَنَّةٌ“ — and it is derived from ”جَنَنْتُ الشَّيْءَ“, said when you have covered something. From this the shield is called ”مِجَنٌّ“, because it covers.

And His saying: ﴿والزَّيْتُونَ والرُّمّانَ مُشْتَبِهًا وغَيْرَ مُتَشابِهٍ﴾, that is: in taste; among it is that whose taste in part resembles the taste of other parts. He paired the olive with the pomegranate because they are two trees of which the Arabs know that their leaves cover the branch from its beginning to its end. The poet said:
؎بُورِكَ المَيِّتُ الغَرِيبُ كَما ∗∗∗ بُورِكَ نَضْرُ الرُّمّانِ والزَّيْتُونِ
(Blessed be the dead man far from home, as the freshness of the pomegranate and the olive is blessed.)
Its meaning is that the blessing is in its leaves and their covering its whole stem.

And His saying: ﴿انْظُرُوا إلى ثَمَرِهِ﴾: one says ”ثَمَرَةٌ“, ”ثَمَرٌ“, ”ثِمارٌ“ and ”ثُمُرٌ“, the plural of ”ثِمارٌ“. So whoever reads ”إلى ثُمُرِهِ“ with ḍamma intends the plural of the plural; and if you wish, you say ”إلى ثَمْرِهِ“ «[Translator's note: so in the text; presumably ”ثُمْرِهِ“ is meant, the ḍamma of the second letter being lightened]», lightening it because of the heaviness of the ḍamma. ﴿وَيَنْعِهِ﴾: ”اَلْيَنْعُ“ is ripeness. One says ”يَنَعَ الشَّجَرُ، وأيْنَعَ“ ("the tree ripened"), when it has matured. The poet said:
؎فِي قِبابٍ حَوْلَ دَسْكَرَةٍ ∗∗∗ حَوْلَها الزَّيْتُونُ قَدْ يَنَعا
(In domed tents around a palace, around which the olive has ripened.)
Abū ʿUbayda said: the verse is by Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya, or by al-Aḥwaṣ.

Allah argued against them by the variation of what He created and its transfer from state to state, by what they know the created cannot do, and [showed] that likewise He will raise them, because they used to deny the resurrection. So He said to them: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكم لآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, and He informed them that in what He has related there is a proof for whoever believes.

zajjaj:100-100.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ الجِنَّ﴾: the meaning is that they obeyed the jinn in the associating of partners which they made attractive to them, and so they made them partners of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Some of them used to ascribe to the jinn acts that belong only to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. So He said: ﴿وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ الجِنَّ وخَلَقَهُمْ﴾. The hāʾ and mīm [of ”خَلَقَهُمْ“], if you wish, refer back to them, that is: they assigned to Allah, who created them, partners who do not create. And it is possible that the hāʾ and mīm refer back to the jinn, so the meaning would be: "They assigned to Allah the jinn as partners, while Allah created the jinn — and how could the partner of Allah be something originated, which was not and then came to be?"

As for the accusative of ”اَلْجِنَّ“, it is from two aspects. One is that ”اَلْجِنَّ“ is a mafʿūl (object), so the meaning would be: "They made the jinn partners to Allah" (”وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ الجِنَّ شُرَكاءَ“), and "partners" would be a second object, as He said: ﴿وَجَعَلُوا المَلائِكَةَ الَّذِينَ هم عِبادُ الرَّحْمَنِ إناثًا﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 19]. And it is possible that ”اَلْجِنَّ“ is a badal (substitute) for ”شُرَكاءَ“ and an explanation of the partners.

And His saying: ﴿وَخَرَقُوا لَهُ بَنِينَ وبَناتٍ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾: the meaning of ”خَرَقُوا“ is: they fabricated and lied. That is because they claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah, the Christians claimed that the Messiah is the son of Allah, and the Jews mentioned that ʿUzayr is the son of Allah. So He, exalted is His praise, made known that they fabricated that without knowledge, that is: they did not state it from knowledge; they only stated it as a lie.

And His saying: ﴿سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى﴾, that is: His freedom from evil. The meaning of ”سُبْحانَهُ“ is declaring [Him] free of every evil. There is no disagreement among the lexicographers about the meaning of tasbīḥ, that it is declaring Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, free [of every imperfection].

zajjaj:101-101.t: And His saying: ﴿بَدِيعُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, that is: He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth. ﴿أنّى يَكُونُ لَهُ ولَدٌ ولَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ صاحِبَةٌ﴾, that is: from where would He have a child, when a child comes only from a consort? ﴿وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾: so He, Majestic and Mighty is He, argued in denying the child that He is the Creator of everything, so nothing is like Him; and how could there be a child for One who has no like? For if a child is ascribed to Him, a like has been made for Him.

zajjaj:103-103.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا تُدْرِكُهُ الأبْصارُ وهو يُدْرِكُ الأبْصارَ﴾: He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He comprehends the sights. In this making known there is an indication that His creatures do not comprehend sight, that is: they do not know what the reality of sight is, nor what the thing is by which a human being has come to see with his eyes rather than seeing with others of his limbs. So He made known that there is a creature among His creatures whose essence the created do not comprehend and whose knowledge they do not encompass; so how then with Him, Mighty and Majestic is He?! Sights do not encompass Him. ﴿وَهُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الخَبِيرُ﴾. As for the reports that have come concerning the seeing [of Allah] and are authentic from the Messenger of Allah, they are not to be rejected, and there is no proof in this verse for rejecting them, because the meaning of this verse is the meaning of comprehending a thing and encompassing its reality. This is the position of the people of the Sunna, of knowledge and of ḥadīth.

zajjaj:104-104.t:
And His saying: ﴿قَدْ جاءَكم بَصائِرُ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾, that is: the Quran has come to you, in which there is clear explanation and insights. So whoever sees, it is for his own soul; the meaning is: "the benefit of that is for his own soul". ﴿وَمَن عَمِيَ فَعَلَيْها﴾, that is: "the harm of that is upon his own soul", because Allah, exalted is His praise, is free of need of His creation.

And His saying: ﴿وَما أنا عَلَيْكم بِحَفِيظٍ﴾, that is: I do not hold you to faith as a guardian and a trustee would. This was before the command to fight; when the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to fight, he became a guardian over them and in control of everyone who turned away.

zajjaj:105-105.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ الآياتِ﴾, that is: and in the like of what We have made clear, We make the signs clear. The position of the kāf at the beginning of ”كَذَلِكَ“ is accusative (naṣb); the meaning is: "And We vary the signs in the like of what We varied them in what has been recited to you" (”وَنُصَرِّفُ الآياتِ في مِثْلِ ما صَرَّفْناهُما فِيما تُلِيَ عَلَيْكَ“). «[Translator's note: the text has the dual pronoun ”صَرَّفْناهُما“; the sense requires ”صَرَّفْناها“ (them, i.e. the signs).]»

And His saying: ﴿وَلِيَقُولُوا دَرَسْتَ﴾: there are five aspects in it. The reading is ”دَرَسْتَ“ with fatḥa on the dāl and fatḥa on the tāʾ, and its meaning is: "and so that they may say: you have read the books of the People of the Book". It is also read ”دارَسْتَ“, that is: "you have studied with the People of the Book". Some said: ”وَلِيَقُولُوا دَرَسَتْ“, that is: these reports that you recite to us are old; they have become effaced (”قَدْ دَرَسْتَ“ «[Translator's note: so vocalised in the text; the sense requires ”دَرَسَتْ“]»), that is: they have passed away and been erased. Al-Akhfash mentioned ”دَرُسَتْ“ with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and its meaning is that of ”دَرَسَتْ“, except that ”دَرُسَتْ“ with ḍamma on the rāʾ is more emphatic. And ”دُرِسَتْ“ with kasra on the rāʾ has been reported, that is: "they have been read".

And His saying: ﴿وَلِنُبَيِّنَهُ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: if someone says: Were the signs varied only so that they would say "you have studied"? The answer to this is that the cause which led them to say ”دَرَسْتَ“ is the recitation of the signs. This lām the lexicographers call "the lām of outcome" (lām al-ṣayrūra). It is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فالتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهم عَدُوًّا وحَزَنًا﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8]: they did not pick him up seeking by taking him that he should become their enemy, but the outcome of his affair was that he became an enemy and a grief to them. And it is as you say: ”كَتَبَ فُلانٌ هَذا الكِتابَ لِحَتْفِهِ“ ("so-and-so wrote this letter to his own death"): he did not intend by the letter to destroy himself, but the outcome was destruction.

zajjaj:107-107.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما أشْرَكُوا﴾, that is: had Allah willed, He would have made them believers. It is said: had Allah willed, He would have sent down to them a sign compelling them to faith. And some said: "had Allah willed, they would not have associated partners", that is: had He willed, He would have uprooted them and so cut off the cause of their associating partners.

zajjaj:13-13.t: And His words: ﴿وَلَهُ ما سَكَنَ في اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ﴾: this too is an argument against the polytheists, because they did not deny that whatever dwells in the night and the day belongs to Allah, i.e. He is its Creator and its Governor; and the One who is like that is able to bring the dead to life.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
Then He added to the argument and the exposition, saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ أغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أتَّخِذُ ولِيًّا فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, i.e. the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

If someone says: His words ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 1] mean "split apart", so how can «الفطر» have the meaning of «الخلق» (creating) while «الانفطار» has the meaning of «الانشقاق» (splitting)? [The answer is that] the two go back to one thing, because the meaning of «فطرهما» is: He created them with a decisive creating, and «الانفطار» and «الفطور» are a breaking apart and a splitting.

And His words: ﴿وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ ولا يُطْعَمُ﴾; it is also read «ولا يَطْعَمُ». The choice among those with insight into Arabic is «وهو يُطعِم ولا يَطعَم», with fatḥa on the yāʾ in the second; they said its meaning is: "He provides and feeds, and does not eat, because He is the Living One, like whom there is nothing". Whoever reads «ولا يُطعَم», the meaning is that He is the Master who provides and is not provided for, just as some slaves provide for their master.

The preferred case in «فاطر» is the genitive (jarr), because it is an attribute of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. The nominative and the accusative are both permissible as praise (madḥ) of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and extolling Him. Whoever puts it in the nominative does so on the implication of «هو», the meaning being: "He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth, and He feeds and is not fed". Whoever puts it in the accusative does so on the meaning of «اذكر» ("mention") and «أعني» ("I mean"). This is an argument against them, because the One who originated the heavens and the earth, brought into being what is in them, made firm their governance and fed those in them, is the One like whom there is nothing.
[Translator's note: the printed text reads «اُذْكُرْ، وأعْنِي بِهَذا الِاحْتِجاجَ عَلَيْهِمْ»; it is rendered here as two implied verbs («اذكر» and «أعني») followed by a new sentence, "This is an argument against them". Read as printed, the last part could also mean "and by this I mean the argument against them".]

zajjaj:16-16.t:
And His words: ﴿مَن يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ﴾, i.e. whoever Allah turns the punishment away from on that day — meaning the Day of Resurrection, in which He mentioned that they will be gathered. It is also read «مَن يُصْرَفُ عنه يومئذٍ فقد رحمه», i.e. whoever has the punishment turned away from him on that day.
[Translator's note: the variant is printed here with «يُصْرَفُ» (nominative verb), the same passive form as the main text; the well-known variant (Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Shuʿba from ʿĀṣim) is the active «مَن يَصْرِفْ عنه», and the author's gloss of the first reading ("whoever Allah turns away") fits that active reading. Translated as printed.]

zajjaj:19-19.t:
And His words: ﴿قُلْ أيُّ شَيْءٍ أكْبَرُ شَهادَةً قُلِ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكُمْ﴾: "the witness" (al-shāhid) is the one who makes clear the claim of the claimant. So Allah, exalted be His praise, commanded His Prophet to argue against them by Allah, the One, who created the heavens and the earth, created the darkness and the light, and created them in stages, as He has made clear in His Book; and He commanded him to make known to them that Allah's testimony that He is One, and the establishment of proofs of His oneness, is the greatest testimony, and that the Qurʾān which he brought testifies for him that he is His Messenger. So He said: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكُمْ﴾ — the One whom you have acknowledged to be the Creator of these things — ﴿وَأُوحِيَ إلَيَّ هَذا القُرْآنُ لأُنْذِرَكم بِهِ﴾.

In the warning there is proof of his prophethood, because no one has brought its like, nor will anyone bring its like; for in it are the reports of past nations, which he brought, upon him be peace, while he was unlettered (ummī), not reading books; and he foretold what would come to pass, and what he foretold proved true. Then He said: ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النّاسِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 67], and he ﷺ was protected from them. And He said: ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ ولَوْ كَرِهَ المُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [al-Tawba: 33], and Allah made the religion of Islam prevail over all other religions, by decisive proof and by the Muslims' prevailing over most regions of the earth. And He said concerning the Jews — who at the time of his mission were the mightiest and most secure of peoples: ﴿وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ والمَسْكَنَةُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 61], so they are abased until the Day of Resurrection.

So Allah foretold in the Qurʾān what has been and what will be, and brought it composed in a composition such that no one among the Arabs was able to produce a single sūra like it — while at the time they were told to bring a sūra like it, they were orators and poets, and there was nothing among them more concise than [their] prose and metrical speech — yet they were incapable of that.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
And His words: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الكِتابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَما يَعْرِفُونَ أبْناءَهُمُ﴾, i.e. they know Muḥammad ﷺ to be a prophet just as they know their sons. It is related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām: "O Abū Ḥamza, did you know Muḥammad as you know your son?" He said: "Yes, because Allah sent His trusted one in His heaven to His trusted one on His earth with his description, so I knew him; as for my son, I do not know what his mother may have done". He said: "You have spoken the truth, O Ḥamza".
[Translator's note: the source addresses Ibn Salām as «أبا حمزة» and then «حمزة»; translated as printed.]

And His words: ﴿الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسَهم فَهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «الذين آتيناهم الكتاب». It may also be as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «فهم لا يؤمنون» as its khabar (predicate). As for ﴿الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾, it is most likely that here it refers to the People of the Book; and it may refer to the whole body of disbelievers, of the People of the Book and others.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
And His words: ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهم إلا أنْ قالُوا﴾: if you wish, you may put «فتنتَهم» in the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «تكن», with «أن قالوا» being the noun (ism) [of «تكن»]; and «تكن» is made feminine although [its noun] is «إلا أن قالوا», because «أن قالوا» here is the fitna. The interpretation of «أن قالوا» may be «إلا مقالتَهم» ("only their saying"). It is also permissible to put the fitna in the nominative with «تكن» feminine, the khabar being «أن قالوا» and the noun «فتنتُهم». It is also permissible to say «ثم لم يكن فتنتَهم إلا أن قالوا», making «يكن» masculine because it is tied to «أن قالوا». And it is permissible to say «ثم لم يكن فتنتُهم», with the yāʾ and the fitna in the nominative, because «الفتنة» and «الافتتان» have one meaning.

The interpretation of this verse is a fine and subtle interpretation in the language, which only someone who knows the meanings of speech and the ways the Arabs handle it can understand. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, mentioned in these narratives what took place concerning the polytheists while they were infatuated (muftatinūn) with their polytheism. Allah made known that their infatuation with their polytheism and their persisting in it amounted to nothing but their disowning it and disclaiming it, so they swore that they had not been polytheists. The like of this in the language is that you see a person loving someone who has gone astray, and when [that one] falls into ruin he disowns him, so you say to him: «ما كانت محبتك لفلان إلا أن انتفيت منه» ("your love for so-and-so was nothing but that you disowned him").

It is permissible to say «والله ربِّنا», with «ربنا» in the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) and praise for His words «والله». It is permissible to say «والله ربَّنا», with «ربنا» in the accusative, the accusative being on two grounds: as an invocation (duʿāʾ): "they said: By Allah, O our Lord, we were not polytheists"; and it may be accusative on [an implied] «أعني», the meaning being "I mean our Lord" and "I mention our Lord". It is also permissible to put it in the nominative on the implication of «هو», being nominative as praise (madḥ). The reading is with the genitive and the accusative; as for the nominative, I know of no one who read it.

zajjaj:108-108.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَسُبُّوا الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾: they were forbidden at that time, before fighting [was prescribed], to curse the idols which the idolaters worship.

﴿فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ عَدْوًا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾, that is: lest they revile Allah out of wrongdoing. Some read: ”فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ عُدُوًّا“, and ”عُدُوًّا“ here is in the sense of "a group", as though it were said: "lest they revile Allah as enemies" (”فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ أعْداءً“); in this view ”عُدُوًّا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ”عَدْوًا“ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), [or] with the lām intended: because the meaning is "so they transgress a transgression" (”فَيَعْتَدُونَ عَدْوًا“), that is, "they wrong a wronging" (”يَظْلِمُونَ ظُلْمًا“); and it may be with the lām intended, that is: "lest they revile Allah for wrongdoing" (”فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ لِلظُّلْمِ“). There is another aspect in it: ”فَيَسُبُّوا اللَّهَ عُدُوًا“, with ḍamma on the dāl, and it is in the sense of ”عُدُوًّا“. Of wrongdoing one says: ”عَدا فُلانٌ عَدْوًا، وعُدُوًّا، وعُدْوانًا، وعَداءً“ ("so-and-so transgressed"), that is: a wrongdoing in which he exceeded the measure.

And His saying, Exalted, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ زَيَّنّا لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ عَمَلَهُمْ﴾: there is more than one view on it. [One is] that it is in the position of "Allah has sealed their hearts", and that is the adorning of their deeds; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَلْ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْها بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 155]. Some said: "We have made their deed fair-seeming to every community", that is: "He has made fair-seeming to every community the deed which is obligatory upon them". The first view is better, because it is in the position of Allah's sealing of their hearts; the proof of that, and the refutation of this [other view], is His saying: ﴿أفَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ فَرَآهُ حَسَنًا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشاءُ ويَهْدِي مَن يَشاءُ﴾ [Fāṭir: 8].

zajjaj:109-109.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَأقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أيْمانِهِمْ﴾, that is: they exerted themselves to the utmost in the oath. ﴿لَئِنْ جاءَتْهم آيَةٌ لَيُؤْمِنُنَّ بِها﴾: they swore only about the signs that they themselves had proposed, for they only said: ﴿لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتّى تَفْجُرَ لَنا مِنَ الأرْضِ يَنْبُوعًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 90], up to His saying: ﴿والمَلائِكَةِ قَبِيلا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 92], that is: you bring them as a surety, that is: they would stand surety. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the signs are with Allah. It is related that the believers said: If a sign were sent down to them, perhaps they would believe. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ إنَّما الآياتُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وما يُشْعِرُكم أنَّها إذا جاءَتْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, that is: and what makes you know? That is: you do not know the unseen, so you do not know that they would believe — as you say to a man, when he says to you "Do such-and-such for me so that I will do such-and-such", something you do not know he will certainly do: ”ما يُدْرِيكَ“ ("what makes you know?").

Then He began anew (istaʾnafa) and said: ﴿أنَّها إذا جاءَتْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾. This is the reading, and it has also been read: ”إنَّها إذا جاءَتْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ“. Sībawayh claimed, on the authority of al-Khalīl, that its meaning is: "perhaps when it comes they will not believe" (”لَعَلَّها إذا جاءَتْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ“), and it is the reading of the people of Madina. Al-Khalīl said: it is like their saying ”إيتِ السُّوقَ أنَّكَ تَشْتَرِي شَيْئًا“ ("go to the market, perhaps you will buy something"), that is: ”لَعَلَّكَ“ (perhaps you). «[Translator's note: so in the text; the "perhaps" interpretation attributed to al-Khalīl belongs to the reading with fatḥa ”أنَّها“, as the following sentences make clear.]» Some said that it is the ”أنْ“ [i.e. ”أنَّ“] in its basic sense, and made ”لا“ redundant (laghw); he said: the meaning is "and what makes you know that when it comes they will believe?" (”وَما يُشْعِرُكم أنَّها إذا جاءَتْ يُؤْمِنُونَ“), as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَحَرامٌ عَلى قَرْيَةٍ أهْلَكْناها أنَّهم لا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 95].

The first view is stronger and better in Arabic, and the kasra is the best and finest of them. The one who mentioned that ”لا“ is redundant is mistaken, because what is redundant cannot be other than redundant: for whoever reads ”إنَّها إذا جاءَتْ“ with kasra on ”إنَّ“, there is consensus that ”لا“ is not redundant, and it is not permissible for the meaning of a single word to be once negation and once affirmation. They are agreed that the meaning of ”أنَّ“ here, when it has fatḥa, is the meaning of ”لَعَلَّ“ (perhaps), and consensus is more worthy of being followed. I have set out the proof in rejection of what was said by the one who claimed that ”لا“ is redundant.

zajjaj:111-111.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّنا نَـزَّلْنا إلَيْهِمُ المَلائِكَةَ وكَلَّمَهُمُ المَوْتى وحَشَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلا ما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: this is the answer to the believers' saying "perhaps they will believe". So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that they will not believe. This is like His informing Nūḥ ﴿أنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إلا مَن قَدْ آمَنَ﴾ [Hūd: 36].

The meaning of ”قُبُلًا“: it is the plural of ”قَبِيلٌ“, and its meaning is "the surety" (al-kafīl), and the meaning would be: "and We gathered against them everything, group by group" (”قَبِيلًا قَبِيلًا“). «[Translator's note: so in the text; the gloss "surety" here seems to belong to the next view, and the meaning "group by group" presupposes qabīl in the sense of "group".]» And it is possible that ”قُبُلٌ“ is the plural of ”قَبِيلٌ“ with the meaning "the surety", and the meaning would be: "if We gathered against them everything, and We made for them [sureties] for the truth of what We say, they would not believe" «[Translator's note: the object of ”نَجْعَلُ“ appears to have dropped from the text; "sureties" is supplied from the context.]». And it is possible that ”قُبُلًا“ is in the sense of "what faces them", that is: "if We gathered against them everything and it faced them". And ”وَحَشَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قِبَلًا“ is permissible, that is: openly before their eyes. And ”قُبْلًا“ is permissible, as a lightening of ”قُبُلٌ“; everything of this pattern may be lightened, such as ”اَلصُّحُفُ“ and ”اَلصُّحْفُ“ (scrolls), ”اَلْكُتُبُ“ and ”اَلْكَتْبُ“ (books) «[Translator's note: so vocalised in the text; the lightened form is ”الكُتْبُ“]», and ”اَلرُّسُلُ“ and ”اَلرُّسْلُ“ (messengers).

The meaning of ”إلّا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ“ is: unless Allah guides them; and it is possible [that it means unless] We send down to them a sign compelling them to faith.

zajjaj:112-112.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا شَياطِينَ الإنْسِ والجِنِّ﴾, that is: just as We have made for you and your community the devils of jinn and men enemies, so We made [them] for the prophets before you and their communities.

”عَدُوًّا“ is in the sense of ”أعْداءً“ (enemies), and ”شَياطِينَ الإنْسِ والجِنِّ“ is accusative as a badal (substitute) from ”عَدُوًّا“, explaining it. And it is possible that ”عَدُوًّا“ is accusative as a second object; the meaning: "and likewise [We made] the devils of jinn and men enemies to the prophets and their communities". ﴿يُوحِي بَعْضُهم إلى بَعْضٍ زُخْرُفَ القَوْلِ غُرُورًا﴾: ”اَلزُّخْرُفُ“ in the language is adornment, and the meaning is that some of them make foul deeds fair-seeming to others. ”غُرُورًا“ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and this maṣdar is carried on the meaning, because the basis of inspiring the adornment of speech is the meaning of deception; it is as though He said: "they deceive a deceiving" (”يَغُرُّونَ غُرُورًا“). ﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ ما فَعَلُوهُ﴾, that is: had Allah willed, He would have prevented the devils from whispering to men and jinn; but Allah tests with what He knows to be most far-reaching in wisdom, most abundant in reward and most beneficial for His servants.

zajjaj:113-113.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلِتَصْغى إلَيْهِ أفْئِدَةُ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالآخِرَةِ﴾: the meaning of ”لِتَصْغى“ is: so that they incline, that is: "and so that their affair comes to that". ”وَلِتُصْغِيَ إلَيْهِ أفْئِدَةُ“ is also permissible. One says ”صَغَوْتُ، أصْغى“ ("I inclined, I incline"), like ”مَحَوْتُ، أمْحى“ ("I erased, I erase"). ”أصْغى“ is permissible — whereas it ought to be ”أصْغُو“ — because of the position of the ghayn, for it and its sisters [the guttural letters] take fatḥa; that is, ”يَفْعُلُ“ and ”يَفْعِلُ“ become ”يَفْعَلُ“ with them in much of the language, as in ”صَبَغَ، يَصْبَغُ“ ("he dyed, he dyes"), whose origin is ”يَصْبُغُ“, which is also said; and like ”ذَهَبَ، يَذْهَبُ“ ("he went, he goes"), as though it had been ”يَذْهُبُ“. One also says ”صَغَيْتُ، أصْغى“; ”أصْغَيْتُ، أصْغى“ is anomalous (shādhdh); and ”أصْغَيْتُ، أُصْغِي“ is good, eloquent and frequent. ”أفْئِدَةٌ“ is the plural of ”فُؤادٌ“ (heart), like ”غُرابٌ“ (crow) and ”أغْرِبَةٌ“.

The meaning of ﴿وَلِيَقْتَرِفُوا ما هم مُقْتَرِفُونَ﴾: it is possible that it is "and so that they do the sins that they are doing"; one says ”قَدِ اقْتَرَفَ فُلانٌ ذَنْبًا“, that is: he has committed a sin. And ”وَلِيَقْتَرِفُوا“ may mean: so that they fabricate and lie. This is the lām of ”أنْ“ [i.e. the lām followed by an implied ”أنْ“]; the meaning is: "and in order that they be pleased with it" (”وَلِأنْ يَرْضَوْهُ“). And [it may be read] ”لْيَقْتَرِفُوا“, the lām being the lām of command, its meaning being threat and menace, as you say ”اِفْعَلْ ما شِئْتَ“ ("do what you like"): its wording is the wording of a command, and its meaning is the meaning of threat.

zajjaj:116-116.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تُطِعْ أكْثَرَ مَن في الأرْضِ يُضِلُّوكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ إنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إلا الظَّنَّ وإنْ هم إلا يَخْرُصُونَ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that most of them are among those who followed their great ones; they do not hold within themselves that they are upon clear insight, but rather they merely conjecture. And among them is one who was obstinate, and one who knows that the Prophet is true.

If someone says: How are they punished when they are only conjecturing? And is it permissible that one who disbelieves while conjecturing is punished, and one who does not disbelieve is upon certainty? The answer to this is that Allah, exalted is His praise, has mentioned that He punishes for conjecture; that is His saying: ﴿وَما خَلَقْنا السَّماءَ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُما باطِلا ذَلِكَ ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنَ النّارِ﴾ [Ṣād: 27]. The proof in this is that they were punished for this conjecture because they followed their desires, abandoned seeking clear insight from where it must be sought, and confined themselves to conjecture and ignorance.

zajjaj:117-117.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ هو أعْلَمُ مَن يَضِلُّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ﴾: the position of ”مَن“ is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject; rafʿ bi-l-ibtidāʾ), and its wording is the wording of interrogation. The meaning is: "Your Lord knows best which of the people strays from His path" (”إنَّ رَبَّكَ هو أعْلَمُ أيُّ النّاسِ يَضِلُّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ“). This is like His saying: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أحْصى لِما لَبِثُوا أمَدًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 12].

zajjaj:118-118.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكُلُوا مِمّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إنْ كُنْتُمْ بِآياتِهِ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: its meaning is: eat of what you have slaughtered purely for Allah; the prohibition of carrion is included in this. There is no disagreement among people that the idolaters disputed with the Muslims and said to them: "You leave what Allah has caused to die before you, and you eat what you yourselves have caused to die."

zajjaj:119-119.t:
So He, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that carrion is forbidden, and that what is slaughtered with the intention of following the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is the lawful. So He said: ﴿وَما لَكم ألا تَأْكُلُوا مِمّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾. The position of ”أنْ“ is accusative (naṣb), because ”في“ has dropped, so the meaning reached ”أنْ“ and put it in the accusative [i.e. accusative by removal of the preposition]. The meaning is: "What is there for you in not eating?" (”أيُّ شَيْءٍ يَقَعُ لَكم في ألّا تَأْكُلُوا؟“). Sībawayh permits the position of ”أنْ“ to be genitive (jarr), even though ”في“ has dropped, but the accusative is better in his view. Abū Isḥāq said: There is no disagreement among people that the position is accusative. ﴿وَقَدْ فَصَّلَ لَكم ما حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ — and ”حُرِّمَ“ [passive] [is read] as well — that is: He has distinguished for you the lawful from the forbidden, and has made lawful to you in necessity what He forbade you.

The position of ”ما“ is accusative in His saying: ﴿إلا ما اضْطُرِرْتُمْ إلَيْهِ﴾. The meaning of ”ما اضْطُرِرْتُمْ“ is: [what] the severity of necessity, that is, the severity of famine, has driven you to eat. ﴿وَإنَّ كَثِيرًا لَيُضِلُّونَ بِأهْوائِهِمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾, that is: those who make carrion lawful and dispute with you about making it lawful — and likewise everything in which they go astray — follow in it only desire and appetite, and they have no insight and no knowledge.

zajjaj:120-120.t: And His saying: ﴿وَذَرُوا ظاهِرَ الإثْمِ وباطِنَهُ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that its outward part is fornication, and its inward part is taking lovers and companions in a suspect manner. What the speech indicates is that the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Leave sin, open or hidden", that is: do not approach what Allah has forbidden you, openly or secretly.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
And His words: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ أكِنَّةً أنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ﴾: «أكنّة» is the plural of «كِنان», which is a covering, like «عِنان» and «أعِنّة». As for «أن يفقهوه», it is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), the meaning being: "and We placed coverings over their hearts out of aversion to their understanding it" («لكراهة أن يفقهوه»). When the lām was omitted, «الكراهة» became accusative, and when «الكراهة» was omitted, its accusative passed to «أن».

And His words: ﴿وَفِي آذانِهِمْ وقْرًا﴾: «الوَقْر» is heaviness of hearing, and it is with fatḥa. One says «في أذنه وَقْر» ("there is deafness in his ear") and «قد وُقِرَت الأذنُ تَوْقَر». The poet said:
؎وَكَلامٍ سَيِّئٍ قَدْ وقَرَتْ ∗∗∗ أُذُنِي مِنهُ وما بِي مِن صَمَمْ
(Many an evil word my ear has been deaf to, though there is no deafness in me.)
And «الوِقْر», with kasra on the wāw, is that a camel or something else carries as much as it can bear. One says «عليه وِقْر» ("he bears a load"), and «نخلة مُوقِر» and «مُوقِرة» ("a heavily laden palm") — with kasra is more common — and «مُوقِر» is like «مُرضِع», i.e. "possessing a load", just as the latter means "possessing suckling".

This was done to them only as a requital for their persisting in their disbelief. The meaning is not that they did not understand it and did not hear it; rather, when they turned away from it and diverted their thought from it — persisting in what they were upon, with its evil outcome — they were in the position of one who has not known and has not heard.

And His words: ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ آيَةٍ لا يُؤْمِنُوا بِها﴾, i.e. every sign that points them to your prophethood. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known the measure of their argumentation and their disputing, and that all they use in argument is to say: "This is the legends of the ancients", and they say: "He has invented a lie against Allah". So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that they do not counter the truth by which the argument against them was made — when they were told: ﴿فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ مِن مِثْلِهِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 23], when He split the moon for them, and when He revealed to His Prophet, upon him be peace: ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النّاسِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 67]. No one brought a sūra, nor was anyone able to harm the Prophet ﷺ or to kill him; and He, Mighty and Majestic, foretold in His Book what would come to pass, and all of that was found [to be so]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿حَتّى إذا جاءُوكَ يُجادِلُونَكَ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إنْ هَذا إلا أساطِيرُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾.

Its singular is «إسطار» and «أسطورة». The interpretation of «السطر» in the language is to make something extended and ordered; of that is «سطر الكتاب» (a line of writing). One says «سَطْر» and «سَطَر». Whoever says «سَطْر» makes its plural «أسطار». Ruʾba said:
؎إنِّي وأسْطارٍ سُطِرْنَ سَطْرا ∗∗∗ لَقائِلٌ يا نَصْرُ نَصْرًا نَصْرا
(By lines that have been written in rows, I am indeed saying: O Naṣr, [give] help, help!)
And the plural of «أسطار» is «أساطير»; on this basis — in my view — is «أساطير الأولين». Whoever says «سَطَر», its plural is «أسطُر», and the plural of the plural is «أساطرة» and «أساطير». Al-Shammākh said, regarding the plural of «سطر»:
؎كَما خَطَّ عِبْرانِيَّةً يَمَنِيَّةً ∗∗∗ بِتَيْماءَ حَبْرٌ ثُمَّ عَرَّضَ أسْطُرا
(As a rabbi in Taymāʾ wrote Hebrew [script], Yemeni [script], then laid the lines across.)
[Translator's note: «إسطار» as the singular of «أساطير» is as printed; the author goes on to derive «أساطير» from «أسطار».]

zajjaj:26-26.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَهم يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ ويَنْأوْنَ عَنْهُ﴾, i.e. [they forbid others] regarding the Prophet ﷺ, that he be followed; «وينأون عنه», i.e. they keep far from him. One says «نأيت عن الشيء أنأى نأيًا» when I am far from it. «النُّؤى» is a barrier made around the tent so that water does not enter it from outside: a small trench is dug around the tent and its earth is placed on the edge of the trench, so the earth prevents the water from entering from outside. It is taken from «النأي», i.e. it keeps the water far from the tent.

Some said that it refers to some of the Prophet's ﷺ kinsfolk, i.e. they forbid harming the Prophet ﷺ yet keep far from him, i.e. they do not follow him. But the speech is connected with the mention of the whole group of the People of the Book and the polytheists, and the first view is closer to the meaning.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His words: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرى إذْ وُقِفُوا عَلى النّارِ﴾: most of the reading is with fatḥa and tafkhīm (full articulation), while imāla (inclination of the vowel) is good and fine, and it is the way of Abū ʿAmr — I mean [inclining] the alif of «النار» towards kasra. Imāla is good in His words ﴿كَمَثَلِ الحِمارِ يَحْمِلُ أسْفارًا﴾ [al-Jumuʿa: 5] and «أصحاب النار» only because the rāʾ after the alif has kasra, and it is a letter that is as though doubled on the tongue, so the kasra on it became like two kasras.

The meaning of ﴿وُقِفُوا عَلى النّارِ﴾ admits three possibilities: it may be that they saw it with their own eyes; it may be that they were over it while it was beneath them; and the best is that the meaning of «وقفوا على النار» is that they were made to enter it and so came to know the measure of its punishment, just as you say in speech «قد وقفتُ على ما عند فلان» ("I have come to know what so-and-so has"), meaning: I have understood it and made it clear to myself.

﴿فَقالُوا يا لَيْتَنا نُرَدُّ ولا نُكَذِّبَ بِآياتِ رَبِّنا ونَكُونَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: most of the readers have the nominative in His words «ولا نكذبُ بآيات ربنا», and the meaning is that they wished to be sent back and guaranteed that they would not deny; the meaning: "Would that we were sent back — and we will not deny the signs of our Lord, whether we are sent back or not", ﴿وَنَكُونَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, i.e. we have seen and witnessed that with which we shall never deny. Sībawayh said its like is «دعني ولا أعود» ("let me go and I will not do it again"), i.e. "and I will not do it again, whether you let me go or not". The nominative is also permissible on another ground, on the meaning: "Would that we were sent back, and would that we did not deny the signs of our Lord", as if they wished for being sent back and for being granted success in believing. In ﴿وَنَكُونَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ the nominative and the accusative are likewise both permissible.

As for the accusative, it is on «يا ليتنا نرد», with «يا ليتنا نرد ولا نكذبَ» being the answer with the wāw after a wish (tamannī), just as you say «ليتك تصير إلينا ونكرمَك» ("would that you came to us and we honoured you"), the meaning being: "would that your coming took place, and our honouring [you]". The meaning would then be: "would that our being sent back took place, and that we did not deny", i.e. "if we were sent back, we would not deny".

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿بَلْ بَدا لَهم ما كانُوا يُخْفُونَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾, i.e. rather, there became apparent to those who followed the misleaders what the misleaders used to hide from them concerning the matter of the resurrection and the raising of the dead, because the connected …
[Translator's note: the source text breaks off here, mid-sentence, at «لِأنَّ المُتَّصِلَ».]

zajjaj:29-29.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقالُوا إنْ هي إلا حَياتُنا الدُّنْيا وما نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ﴾: they denied the resurrection in order to embolden [themselves] to sins; and even if they were sent back, they would return to what they had been forbidden. Some said: if they were sent back without having seen the punishment, they would return — as if he holds that they had not witnessed what would compel them to desist. And this — «عَلَّهُ» — is clear, because this saying of theirs comes after they had been resurrected, had learned the matter of the Resurrection and had seen the Fire. So the meaning is that most of those of the Jews and the polytheists who saw [the truth] knew that Allah's command is true, yet inclined towards ease and [thought] that the matter was deferred from them to a term, as Iblīs did, who had witnessed of Allah's proofs that beyond which there is no further limit. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that if they were sent back they would return, because they disbelieved after the proof had become binding upon them.
[Translator's note: the printed text reads «وهَذا - عَلَّهُ - بَيِّنٌ», which is unclear; it may be a corruption of «وهذا غلطٌ بيّن» ("and this is a clear error"), which fits the author's rebuttal that follows. Rendered tentatively.]

Some of the commentators said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked; it was said to him: "What is the matter with the people of the Fire — they did the deeds of the people of the Fire in a short lifetime and are made to abide forever in the Fire; and the people of the Garden did the deeds of the people of the Garden in a short lifetime and are made to abide forever in the Garden?" He said: "Each of the two parties was such that, had it lived forever, it would have done that deed".

zajjaj:31-31.t:
And His words: ﴿قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقاءِ اللَّهِ حَتّى إذا جاءَتْهُمُ السّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً﴾: everything that comes suddenly has «بَغَت»; one says «قد بغته الأمر يبغته بغتًا وبغتةً» when it comes upon him suddenly. The poet said:
؎وَلَكِنَّهم ماتُوا ولَمْ أخْشَ بَغْتَةً ∗∗∗ وأفْظَعُ شَيْءٍ حِينَ يَفْجَؤُكَ البَغْتُ
(But they died, and I feared no sudden blow — and the most dreadful thing is when the sudden strikes you unawares.)

And His words: ﴿يا حَسْرَتَنا عَلى ما فَرَّطْنا فِيها﴾: if someone says, "What is the meaning of calling upon regret (ḥasra), when it neither understands nor answers?", the answer to that is that when the Arabs exert themselves in reporting some grave matter they have fallen into, they make it a vocative (nidāʾ); so its wording is the wording of something being alerted, while the one alerted is someone else — like His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا حَسْرَتا عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ في جَنْبِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 56], and His words: ﴿يا ويْلَتى أألِدُ وأنا عَجُوزٌ﴾ [Hūd: 72], and His words: ﴿يا ويْلَنا مَن بَعَثَنا مِن مَرْقَدِنا هَذا﴾ [Yā Sīn: 52]. This is more eloquent than saying «أنا حَسِرٌ على العباد» ("I feel regret for the servants") and more eloquent than saying «الحسرة علينا في تفريطنا» ("regret is upon us for our neglect"). Sībawayh said: when you say «يا عجباه», it is as if you said: "Be present and come, O wonder, for this is one of your times".
[Translator's note: «فإنه من أزمانك» is as printed; the sense "this is one of your times/occasions" is assumed.]
The interpretation of «يا حسرتنا» is: "Take notice that we have lost". The like of this in speech, in that you bring «يا» upon it for alerting while you mean the people, is your saying «لا أرينّك ههنا» ("let me not see you here"): your wording is the wording of one forbidding himself, but since it is known that a person has no need to utter a prohibition to himself, the one addressed enters into the prohibition, so the meaning becomes: "Do not be here, for if you are, I will see you". Likewise «يا حسرتنا»: it is known that regret is not called upon, so the alerting falls upon those addressed. The meaning of «فرطنا فيها» is: we put forward incapacity.

And His words: ﴿وَهم يَحْمِلُونَ أوْزارَهُمْ﴾, i.e. they carry the weight of their sins. This is a figurative expression (mathal); it may be that what befalls them of punishment has been made like the heaviest thing that is carried, because heaviness (al-thiql) is used both for a burden and for a state. You say of a state: «قد ثقل عليّ خطاب فلان» ("so-and-so's speech has weighed heavily on me"), whose interpretation is: "I have disliked his speech with a dislike that has grown hard upon me". So the interpretation of «الوزر» is «الثقل» from this angle. Its derivation is from «الوَزَر», which is the mountain, that in which the king and the prophet take refuge, i.e. that which helps him; of it is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا مَعَهُ أخاهُ هارُونَ وزِيرًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 35] — Mūsā asked his Lord to make his brother a vizier (wazīr) for him.

Likewise His words, Exalted is He: ﴿ألا ساءَ ما يَزِرُونَ﴾, i.e. evil is the thing as a thing, i.e. that which they carry. We have explained the operation of «نعم» and «بئس» earlier in the book. Likewise ﴿ساءَ مَثَلا القَوْمُ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 177], i.e. the likeness of the people.

zajjaj:121-121.t: And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلا تَأْكُلُوا مِمّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾, that is: of what has not been slaughtered purely for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ﴾: the meaning of ”اَلْفِسْقُ“ is going out from the truth and the religion. One says ”فَسَقَتِ الرُّطَبَةُ“ ("the ripe date has come out"), when it comes out of its skin. ﴿وَإنَّ الشَّياطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إلى أوْلِيائِهِمْ لِيُجادِلُوكُمْ﴾, that is: the devil whispers to his ally and casts into his heart disputation with falsehood; that is what we have described, that the idolaters disputed with the Muslims about carrion. ﴿وَإنْ أطَعْتُمُوهم إنَّكم لَمُشْرِكُونَ﴾: in this verse there is a proof that everyone who makes lawful something that Allah has forbidden him, or forbids something that Allah has made lawful for him, is an associator (mushrik). If someone made carrion lawful without necessity, or made fornication lawful, he would be an associator by the consensus of the community, even if he obeyed Allah in all that He commanded. He is called "an associator" only because he followed other than Allah, and so associated another with Allah.

zajjaj:122-122.t: And His saying: ﴿أوَمَن كانَ مَيْتًا فَأحْيَيْناهُ وجَعَلْنا لَهُ نُورًا يَمْشِي بِهِ في النّاسِ كَمَن مَثَلُهُ في الظُّلُماتِ لَيْسَ بِخارِجٍ مِنها﴾: it has come in the exegesis that by it are meant the Prophet ﷺ and Abū Jahl ibn Hishām. The Prophet ﷺ was guided and given the light of Islam, prophethood and wisdom, while Abū Jahl was in the darknesses of disbelief. It is possible that this verse is general, for everyone whom Allah has guided and everyone whom Allah has led astray. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that the likeness of the rightly guided is the likeness of the dead one who was brought to life and made to have light, walking among people by the light of wisdom and faith; and the likeness of the disbeliever is the likeness of one who is in the darknesses and does not get free of them.

zajjaj:123-123.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنا في كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أكابِرَ مُجْرِمِيها لِيَمْكُرُوا فِيها﴾: the position of the kāf is accusative (naṣb), conjoined to what precedes it, which is His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْكافِرِينَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 122]. The meaning is: "Like that which We have related to you, their deeds were made fair-seeming to the disbelievers"; ”وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنا“, that is: "and like that We placed in every town its greatest criminals, to plot in it", because the leadership and affluence in which the great ones are is more conducive to plotting and disbelief for them. The proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبادِهِ لَبَغَوْا في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 27].

And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلا أنْ يَكُونَ النّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفًا مِن فِضَّةٍ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33]. And the meaning of ﴿وَما يَمْكُرُونَ إلا بِأنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ is: that plotting rebounds upon them, because they are punished for their plotting.

zajjaj:124-124.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَإذا جاءَتْهم آيَةٌ﴾: this hāʾ and mīm refer back to the great ones who have been mentioned, because they said: We will not believe until we are given signs like those the prophets were given. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He knows best who is fit, and He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْناهم عَلى عِلْمٍ عَلى العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 32].

And His saying: ﴿اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رِسالَتَهُ﴾, that is: He knows best whom to single out for the message. Some said: [belief] in the messengers does not reach completeness unless, before being sent, they were obeyed among their people, because [otherwise] there would be wide room for attacking them. And it is said: they were only great ones and leaders, and so they were followed. ﴿سَيُصِيبُ الَّذِينَ أجْرَمُوا صَغارٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: even if they were great ones in this world, humiliation (ṣaghār), that is abasement, will strike them with Allah. ”عِنْدَ“ is connected with [the verb]: "humiliation will strike them with Allah" (”سَيُصِيبُهم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ صَغارٌ“); and it is possible that ”عِنْدَ“ is connected with ”صَغارٌ“, so the meaning would be: "a humiliation established for them with Allah will strike those who committed crimes". It is not valid that ”مِن“ has been omitted from ”عِنْدَ“ [i.e. that it means "from Allah"]; [the meaning of] "from" (”مِن عِنْدِ“) is what is omitted in meaning only when you say ”زَيْدٌ عِنْدَ عَمْرٍو“ ("Zayd is with ʿAmr"), and the meaning is "Zayd is in the presence of ʿAmr". «[Translator's note: the last sentence is obscure in the text as transmitted; it is rendered literally.]»

zajjaj:125-125.t:
﴿فَمَن يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أنْ يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلإسْلامِ﴾: it is related from Ibn Masʿūd that he asked the Prophet ﷺ: Does the breast become expanded? He said: "Yes, light enters the heart." Ibn Masʿūd said: Is there a sign of that? He said: "Yes: shunning the abode of delusion, turning to the abode of eternity, and preparing for death before death."

﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ أنْ يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا﴾: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: ”اَلْحَرَجُ“ is a place of intertwined trees; so it is as though wisdom does not reach the heart of the disbeliever, just as grazing animals do not reach the place where the trees are intertwined. The lexicographers also say this: intertwined trees are called ”اَلْحَرَجُ“; and ”اَلْحَرَجُ“ in the language is the narrowest narrowness. What Ibn ʿAbbās said is sound and good; the meaning according to the lexicographers is that it is very narrow. ”حَرِجًا“ with kasra on the rāʾ is also permissible. Whoever says ”حَرِجًا“ — it is in the position of their saying ”رَجُلٌ دَنِفٌ“ ("a man gravely ill"), because your saying ”دَنَفٌ“ here, and ”حَرَجٌ“, are not active participles (asmāʾ al-fāʿilīn); it is only in the position of their saying ”رَجُلٌ عَدْلٌ“ ("a just man"), that is: "a man possessing justice". «[Translator's note: the text appears to be compressed: the forms with fatḥa (”دَنَفٌ“, ”حَرَجٌ“) are maṣdars used descriptively, like ”عَدْلٌ“, while ”دَنِفٌ“ and ”حَرِجٌ“ with kasra are adjectives.]»

And His saying: ﴿كَأنَّما يَصَّعَّدُ في السَّماءِ﴾ — and ”يَصّاعَدُ“ as well — its origin is ”يَتَصاعَدُ“ and ”يَتَصَعَّدُ“, except that the tāʾ is assimilated into the ṣād because of its closeness to it. The meaning of ”كَأنَّما يَصَّعَّدُ في السَّماءِ“ — and Allah knows best — is: as though he had been charged with climbing up to the sky when he is called to Islam, because of the narrowness of his breast towards it. And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that it means: as though his heart rises into the sky in aversion to Islam and to hearing wisdom. ﴿كَذَلِكَ يَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ الرِّجْسَ عَلى الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, that is: like what We relate to you, Allah lays defilement (al-rijs) upon those who do not believe. ”اَلرِّجْسُ“ is the curse in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:127-127.t: And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَهم دارُ السَّلامِ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾, that is: for the believers is the Abode of Peace. Some said: ”اَلسَّلامُ“ is one of the names of Allah, and its proof is: ﴿السَّلامُ المُؤْمِنُ المُهَيْمِنُ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 23]. And it is possible that Paradise was called "the Abode of Peace" (dār al-salām) because it is the abode of everlasting safety that is never cut off.

zajjaj:128-128.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهم جَمِيعًا يا مَعْشَرَ الجِنِّ﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: then it will be said to them: ﴿يا مَعْشَرَ الجِنِّ قَدِ اسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ مِنَ الإنْسِ﴾; the meaning is: you have taken many of mankind whom you led astray. ﴿وَقالَ أوْلِياؤُهم مِنَ الإنْسِ رَبَّنا اسْتَمْتَعَ بَعْضُنا بِبَعْضٍ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that mankind's enjoyment of the jinn was that a man, when he travelled on a journey and became afraid, or caught game, would say: "I seek refuge in the Lord of this valley, and in the master of this valley," meaning by it the jinn. And the jinn's enjoyment of mankind was that the human had acknowledged to him that he was able to defend him. What the wording indicates — and Allah knows best — is mankind's acceptance from the jinn of that with which they used to lead them astray, because of His saying: ﴿اسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ مِنَ الإنْسِ﴾; as for those who used to say this — I mean, seek refuge with the jinn — they were few. ﴿قالَ النّارُ مَثْواكُمْ﴾: ”اَلْمَثْوى“ is the place of abiding. ﴿خالِدِينَ فِيها﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "the Fire is your abode, in a state of everlasting abiding".

And His saying: ﴿إلا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: the meaning of the exception (istithnāʾ) here in my view — and Allah knows best — is only from the Day of Resurrection, because His saying ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهم جَمِيعًا﴾ is the Day of Resurrection. So He said: "abiding in it from when they are raised, except what your Lord wills of the length of their gathering from their graves and the length of their time in being called to account." And it is possible that it is: "except what Allah wills to punish them with of the kinds of punishment", as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿لَهم فِيها زَفِيرٌ وشَهِيقٌ﴾ [Hūd: 106] ﴿خالِدِينَ فِيها ما دامَتِ السَّماواتُ والأرْضُ إلا ما شاءَ رَبُّكَ﴾ [Hūd: 107]. So it is possible — and Allah knows best — [that it means] "except what your Lord wills of the length of their gathering and their reckoning", and it is possible that it is "except what your Lord wills of the punishment by which He increases them".

And His saying: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾, that is: He is wise in what He has made their recompense, and wise in other than it.

zajjaj:130-130.t: And His saying: ﴿يا مَعْشَرَ الجِنِّ والإنْسِ ألَمْ يَأْتِكم رُسُلٌ مِنكم يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكم آياتِي﴾: He said "messengers from among you", whereas the one sent is only from mankind, not from the jinn. That is permissible only because the group is rational and is addressed, so the messengers are some of those who are rational. This is like His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنهُما اللُّؤْلُؤُ والمَرْجانُ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 22], whereas that comes out only from the salt [water], that is, the sea that is not fresh; yet He said ”مِنهُما“ ("from the two of them"), because mention of them both had been joined together. This is permissible in the language in everything that agrees in its origin, just as the jinn agree with mankind in the matter of discernment (tamyīz).

zajjaj:131-131.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ أنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ رَبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ القُرى﴾: Sībawayh claimed that the position of ”ذَلِكَ“ is nominative (rafʿ); the meaning is: "The matter is that, because your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly." Some said: its position may be accusative (naṣb); the meaning is: "That was said because your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly."
