The meaning comes out under both views, because the meaning points to the matter of sending [messengers]; so it is as though — and Allah knows best — [it were]: "That which We have related to you of the affair of the messengers [and] the affair of the punishment of whoever denied them is because He would not destroy the towns unjustly", that is: He does not destroy them until He sends them a messenger, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَما كُنّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 15].

zajjaj:133-133.t:
And His saying: ﴿كَما أنْشَأكم مِن ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ﴾: the position of the kāf is accusative (naṣb); the meaning is: "and He causes whomever He wills to succeed after you, just as He produced you" (”وَيَسْتَخْلِفُ مِن بَعْدِكم ما يَشاءُ مِثْلَما أنْشَأكم“). One says ”أنْشَأ اللَّهُ الخَلْقَ“ ("Allah produced creation") when He created it and originated it. Everyone who begins something has "produced" it (anshaʾahu); from that is your saying ”فَأنْشَأ الشّاعِرُ يَقُولُ“ ("then the poet began to say"), that is: he began from himself. ”اَلنَّشَأُ“ are the small ones among children. Nuṣayb said:
؎وَلَوْلا أنْ يُقالَ صَبا نُصَيْبٌ ∗∗∗ لَقُلْتُ بِنَفْسِيَ النَّشَأُ الصِّغارُ
(Were it not that it would be said "Nuṣayb has fallen into youthful passion", I would say: my soul be ransom for the young little ones.)
For this reason one says of small children: ”نَشْءٌ حَسَنٌ“ and ”نُشُوءٌ حَسَنٌ“ ("a fine growth"), that is: a fine beginning has appeared for him.

zajjaj:33-33.t: And His words: ﴿فَإنَّهم لا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ﴾, and [it is also read] «لا يُكْذِبُونَكَ». The meaning of «كذّبته» is: I said to him "you have lied"; and the meaning of «أكذبته» is: I claimed that what he brought is a lie. The explanation of His words «لا يكذّبونك» is: they are not able to say to you "you have lied" concerning what you have reported of what is in their books. Another aspect: they do not deny you in their hearts, i.e. they know that you are truthful, ﴿وَلَكِنَّ الظّالِمِينَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ﴾, because what they rejected was only the proofs of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. It is also possible that «فإنهم لا يكذبونك» means: "you are truthful in their eyes", because he ﷺ used to be called among them "al-Amīn" (the Trustworthy) before the mission; but they rejected with their tongues that in which their hearts bore witness to their lying.

zajjaj:34-34.t: Then Allah consoled His Prophet and gave him patience by informing him that the messengers before him had been denied by nations, saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ مِن قَبْلِكَ فَصَبَرُوا عَلى ما كُذِّبُوا وأُوذُوا حَتّى أتاهم نَصْرُنا ولا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِماتِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. since Allah said to His Messenger: ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النّاسِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 67], and since He said: ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 33], there is no changer of Allah's words, i.e. Allah does not break His promise, and no one overcomes His allies.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known to His Messenger that He brings whatever signs He loves, and that he ﷺ is a human being who is not able to bring a sign except such signs as Allah wills. So He said: ﴿وَإنْ كانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكَ إعْراضُهُمْ﴾, i.e. if it has weighed heavily on you that they turned away when they asked you to bring down an angel upon them — for they said: ﴿لَوْلا أُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 8]. Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that even if the angels came down upon them and some mighty sign came to them, they would not believe.

And His words: ﴿فَإنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أنْ تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقًا في الأرْضِ﴾: «النَّفَق» is a passage that runs through the ground. «النافِقاء» — with the long ending (mamdūd) — is one of the burrows of the jerboa, which it bores from deep in the ground up to the skin of the ground; when it reaches the skin it makes it thin, so that if some creeping thing alarms it, it pushes up that spot with its head and comes out through it. From this the «منافق» (hypocrite) was called «منافق», because he concealed something other than what he displayed, like the «نافقاء», whose outside is not visible while its inside is a hole dug in the ground.

And His words: ﴿أوْ سُلَّمًا في السَّماءِ﴾: «السُّلَّم» (ladder) is derived from «السلامة» (safety); it is the thing that delivers you safely to your place of ascent. The meaning is: "if you are able to do this, then do it". «فافعل» ("then do it") is not in the Qurʾān, because what the speech gives an indication of may be omitted. Like that is your saying: «إن رأيت أن تمضي معنا إلى فلان ولا تذكرَ فافعل» ("if you see fit to go with us to so-and-so and not mention [it], then do so"). So Allah made known to His Prophet ﷺ that he cannot bring a sign except by Allah's permission; and His making this known to the Prophet is making known to creation that it was they who proposed the signs. And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that He is able to send down sign after sign, and that even if the angels were sent down and the dead spoke to them, they would not believe unless Allah willed.

And His words: ﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَمَعَهم عَلى الهُدى﴾: there is more than one view on it. One of them is that had Allah willed to stamp them with guidance He would have done so. Another view: «ولو شاء الله لجمعهم على الهدى», i.e. had He willed He would have sent down upon them a sign compelling them to faith, like His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إنْ نَشَأْ نُنَـزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أعْناقُهم لَها خاضِعِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 4]. Allah only sent down signs alongside which people reflect, so that the one with insight is rewarded and recompensed for believing in the signs; had fire come down upon whoever disbelieved, or had he been pelted with a stone from the sky, everyone would have believed.

zajjaj:36-36.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إنَّما يَسْتَجِيبُ الَّذِينَ يَسْمَعُونَ﴾, i.e. those who hear with the hearing of those who accept; and He made whoever does not accept like the deaf. The poet said:
؎أصَمُّ عَمّا ساءَهُ سَمِيعُ
(Deaf to whatever displeases him, [yet] keen of hearing.)
﴿والمَوْتى يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾, i.e. He brings them to life, ﴿ثُمَّ إلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ﴾.

zajjaj:37-37.t: And His words: ﴿قُلْ إنَّ اللَّهَ قادِرٌ عَلى أنْ يُنَـزِّلَ آيَةً﴾, i.e. a sign that would unite them upon guidance.

zajjaj:38-38.t: And His words: ﴿وَما مِن دابَّةٍ في الأرْضِ ولا طائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَناحَيْهِ﴾: «ولا طائرٌ» in the nominative is permissible, by conjunction with the position of «دابّة», the interpretation being: «وما دابّةٌ في الأرض ولا طائرٌ». The genitive is better and more prevalent, on the meaning «وما من دابّةٍ ولا طائرٍ». He said «يطير بجناحيه» ("flying with its two wings") by way of tawkīd (emphasis), because you may say to a man «طِرْ في حاجتي» ("fly to my need"), i.e. hurry. Everything Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has created is not free of one of these two states: either it creeps or it flies. ﴿إلا أُمَمٌ أمْثالُكُمْ﴾, i.e. in creation, death and resurrection.

zajjaj:40-40.t:
And His words: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتَكم إنْ أتاكم عَذابُ اللَّهِ أوْ أتَتْكُمُ السّاعَةُ﴾: «الساعة» (the Hour) is a name for the time in which the servants are struck down, and a name for the time in which the servants are resurrected. The meaning is: if the Hour comes to you in which you were promised resurrection and extinction — because before the resurrection is the death of all creation.

And His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ﴾, i.e. do you call upon these idols and stones which you have worshipped besides Allah? So Allah argued against them with what they cannot repel, because when harm touched them they used to call upon Allah.

The grammarians have said more than one thing about this kāf in His words «أرأيتكم». Al-Farrāʾ said: its form is the form of an accusative, while its interpretation is that of a nominative. He said: like it is the kāf in the saying «دونك زيدًا» ("here, take Zayd"); he said: the kāf is in the position of a genitive (khafḍ), while its interpretation is that of the nominative, because the meaning is «خذ زيدًا» ("take Zayd"). This was not said by any of the earlier grammarians, and it is an error, because in your saying «أرأيتك زيدًا ما شأنه؟» «أرأيت» would then have passed over to the kāf and to Zayd, so «رأيت» would have two nouns [as objects], and the meaning would become: "Have you seen yourself Zayd — what is his state?", and this is absurd. What the grammarians whose knowledge is trusted hold is that the kāf has no position [in i'rab], and the meaning is only «أرأيت زيدًا ما حاله؟» ("have you considered Zayd — what is his state?"); the kāf is merely an addition to make the address clear, and it is what the address relies on.

Know that — when the kāf is added for address — you say to a single male: «أرأيتَكَ زيدًا ما حاله؟», with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the kāf. To a female you say: «أرأيتَكِ زيدًا ما حاله يا امرأةُ», keeping the fatḥa [on the tāʾ] according to the base form of addressing a male, and putting kasra on the kāf, because it has become the last thing in the word and the one that makes the address clear. To two you say «أرأيتَكُما زيدًا ما حاله؟», and «أرأيتَكم زيدًا ما حاله» for a group: you keep the tāʾ singular; and just as you must keep it singular in the dual and plural, you must keep it masculine with the feminine. If you ask women, you say «أرأيتَكُنّ زيدًا ما حاله؟». The feminine dual is like the masculine dual in everything.

If, in this chapter, you make the agent pass over to the object, the kāf becomes its object. You say «رأيتُني عالمًا بفلان» ("I considered myself knowledgeable about so-and-so"); and if you ask about it on this condition, you say to a man: «أرأيتَكَ عالمًا بفلان؟». On this basis you say to two: «أرأيتاكما عالمَين بفلان؟», and to a group: «أرأيتموكم عالمين بفلان؟», because this is in the interpretation of «أرأيتم أنفسكم؟» ("have you considered yourselves?"). To a woman you say «أرأيتِكِ عالمةً بفلان», with kasra on the tāʾ and the kāf; to two you say «أرأيتُماكما عالمَين بفلان؟», and to a group [of women] «أرأيتَكُنّ عالماتٍ بفلان؟». On this is the analogy of these two chapters.
[Translator's note: in the second paradigm the dual is printed in two different forms («أرأيتاكما» and «أرأيتماكما»), and the feminine plural is printed «أرأيتَكُنّ», identical to the first paradigm (where the tāʾ is kept singular), although in this paradigm the agent and object are both marked, as «أرأيتموكم» shows. All forms are translated as printed.]

zajjaj:41-41.t:
And His words: ﴿بَلْ إيّاهُ تَدْعُونَ﴾: «بل» is istidrāk (correction) and affirmation after negation; you say «ما جاء زيدٌ بل عمرٌو» ("Zayd did not come, rather ʿAmr"). So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known to them that in times of hardship they call upon none but Him, and in that is the greatest argument against them, because they had worshipped idols.

And His words: ﴿فَيَكْشِفُ ما تَدْعُونَ إلَيْهِ إنْ شاءَ﴾: the meaning is: He removes the harm on account of which you called. This is by way of expansiveness in speech (ittisāʿ al-kalām), like «سل القرية» ("ask the town"), the meaning being "ask the people of the town".

And His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَتَنْسَوْنَ ما تُشْرِكُونَ﴾: «وتنسون» here is of two kinds: it may be that «تنسون» means "you abandon"; and it may be that the meaning is: "in your abandoning calling upon them you are like those who are heedless (yashūna)".

zajjaj:42-42.t: And His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أرْسَلْنا إلى أُمَمٍ مِن قَبْلِكَ فَأخَذْناهم بِالبَأْساءِ والضَّرّاءِ﴾: it has been said that «البأساء» is hunger, and «الضرّاء» is loss in wealth and lives. The meaning is that Allah, exalted be His praise, made known to His Prophet ﷺ that He had sent messengers before him to people who had reached such hardness [of heart] that they were seized with severity in their persons and their wealth, so that they might submit and humble themselves to Allah's command — because hearts become humble and souls become submissive when something of Allah's command comes in the form of misery and adversity — yet they did not become humble and did not become submissive. He said: ﴿لَعَلَّهم يَتَضَرَّعُونَ﴾. The meaning of «لعلّ» is hope (tarajjī), and this hope is on the part of the servants: Allah seized them with that so that what the servants would hope for from it is humble supplication, just as He, Mighty and Majestic, said in the story of Pharaoh: ﴿لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أوْ يَخْشى﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 44]. Sībawayh said: the meaning is "go, the two of you, in your hope", while Allah knows what will come after that.

zajjaj:43-43.t: And His words: ﴿فَلَوْلا إذْ جاءَهم بَأْسُنا تَضَرَّعُوا﴾: the meaning is: why then, when Our might came to them, did they not humble themselves? ﴿وَلَكِنْ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾, i.e. they persisted in their disbelief.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
And His words: ﴿فَلَمّا نَسُوا ما ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ فَتَحْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أبْوابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾, i.e. We opened to them the gates of every good thing that had been closed to them, ﴿حَتّى إذا فَرِحُوا بِما أُوتُوا﴾, i.e. until, when they thought that all that had befallen them had not been vengeance from Allah, Majestic and Mighty — and when [things] were opened to them they thought that this was by their own deserving — ﴿أخَذْناهم بَغْتَةً﴾, i.e. Our punishment took them by surprise from where they did not perceive.

And His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإذا هم مُبْلِسُونَ﴾: «المُبْلِس» is one in intense regret, despairing and grieving.

zajjaj:45-45.t: And His words: ﴿فَقُطِعَ دابِرُ القَوْمِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا والحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, praised Himself for cutting off their last remnant and uprooting them entirely, because He, Majestic and Mighty, had sent messengers to them, granted them respite after their disbelief, and seized them with misery and adversity; so He, Majestic and Mighty, went to the utmost in warning them and giving them respite. So He praised Himself, because He is praiseworthy in giving respite to whoever disbelieves in Him and in awaiting his repentance.

zajjaj:46-46.t:
And His words: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ أخَذَ اللَّهُ سَمْعَكم وأبْصارَكم وخَتَمَ عَلى قُلُوبِكم مَن إلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَأْتِيكم بِهِ﴾, i.e. with your hearing; and what is conjoined to «السمع» is included in the account, since it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «السمع».

And His words: ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ الآياتِ ثُمَّ هم يَصْدِفُونَ﴾, i.e. "they turn away". Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that He varies the signs for them — these being the indications that point to His oneness and to the soundness of His Prophet's ﷺ prophethood — then they turn away from what has become clear to them and evident before them.

zajjaj:47-47.t: And His words: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتَكم إنْ أتاكم عَذابُ اللَّهِ بَغْتَةً أوْ جَهْرَةً﴾: «البغتة» is taking by surprise, and «الجهر» is: or it comes to them while they see it. ﴿هَلْ يُهْلَكُ إلا القَوْمُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾, i.e. will any be destroyed but you and those like you? For you disbelieved obstinately, and so you know that you are wrongdoers.

zajjaj:48-48.t: And His words: ﴿وَما نُرْسِلُ المُرْسَلِينَ إلا مُبَشِّرِينَ ومُنْذِرِينَ﴾, i.e. their being sent is not so that they bring people the signs that they propose to them; they bring only such signs by which Allah makes their proofs clear, and their aim is only giving good tidings and warning.

zajjaj:50-50.t:
And His words: ﴿قُلْ لا أقُولُ لَكم عِنْدِي خَزائِنُ اللَّهِ﴾: this is connected with His words: ﴿لَوْلا نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِن رَبِّهِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 37]. So the Prophet ﷺ made known to them that he does not possess Allah's treasuries, by which He provides and gives, and that he does not know the unseen, so as to inform them of what is hidden from him of what has passed and what will be, except by revelation from Allah, Majestic and Mighty. ﴿وَلا أقُولُ لَكم إنِّي مَلَكٌ﴾, i.e. the angel witnesses of the affairs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, what human beings do not witness. So he made known to them that he follows revelation, saying: ﴿إنْ أتَّبِعُ إلا ما يُوحى إلَيَّ﴾, i.e. whatever of the unseen I have told you concerning what has passed and what will be is by revelation from Allah. As for telling of what has passed, it is reporting the stories of past nations; and reporting what will be is like His words: ﴿غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ﴾ [al-Rūm: 2] ﴿فِي أدْنى الأرْضِ وهم مِن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ﴾ [al-Rūm: 3] ﴿فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ﴾ [al-Rūm: 4] — and what he foretold of that came to pass — and like His words: ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النّاسِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 67]: they strove to kill him and did not attain that.

And His words: ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 33]. And the reports related from him about what will be are too many to count.

And His words: ﴿وَأنْذِرْ بِهِ الَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ أنْ يُحْشَرُوا إلى رَبِّهِمْ لَيْسَ لَهم مِن دُونِهِ ولِيٌّ ولا شَفِيعٌ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 51]: His words «وأنذر به», i.e. with the Qurʾān. Those who fear the gathering are mentioned, rather than others — while he ﷺ is the warner of all creation — only because the argument is more binding upon those who fear the gathering, since they have a better understanding of the appointed return. They are one of two men: either a Muslim man, who fulfils Allah's right in his Islam; or a man of the People of the Book — and the People of the Book all acknowledge that Allah, exalted be His praise, is their Creator and that they will be resurrected.

And His words: ﴿لَيْسَ لَهم مِن دُونِهِ ولِيٌّ ولا شَفِيعٌ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 51]: because the Christians and the Jews claimed that they were the sons of Allah and His beloved; so Allah made known that He has no allies but the believers, and that the people of disbelief have, besides Allah, no ally and no intercessor.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
And His words: ﴿وَلا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهم بِالغَداةِ والعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وجْهَهُ﴾: some of the polytheists wanted to use a stratagem against the Prophet ﷺ, so they said: "If you were to keep these lowly people and slaves away from you, the great men and the nobles would sit with you". By those whom they reckoned the Prophet ﷺ would keep away they meant Ṣuhayb, Khabbāb, ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, Salmān al-Fārisī and Bilāl. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the matter of religion takes precedence, forbade him to keep these away, and made known to him that they seek what is with Allah. So He testified to the soundness of their intentions and that they are sincere to Allah in that, saying: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ وجْهَهُ﴾, i.e. they seek Allah and aim for the paths He commanded them to aim for. By this they only reckoned that he would keep them away, so that they would have an argument against him. And Allah has made known in the story of Nūḥ that those who followed Nūḥ were those whom [his people] regarded as the lowest of them; He said: ﴿قالُوا أنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ واتَّبَعَكَ الأرْذَلُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 111], and they said: ﴿وَما نَراكَ اتَّبَعَكَ إلا الَّذِينَ هم أراذِلُنا﴾ [Hūd: 27].

And His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ is the answer (jawāb) to ﴿وَلا تَطْرُدِ﴾.

And His words «فتطردهم» is the answer to ﴿ما عَلَيْكَ مِن حِسابِهِمْ مِن شَيْءٍ وما مِن حِسابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن شَيْءٍ فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ﴾.

zajjaj:53-53.t: The meaning of ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ فَتَنّا بَعْضَهم بِبَعْضٍ﴾ is: We tested and tried. ﴿لِيَقُولُوا أهَؤُلاءِ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن بَيْنِنا﴾, i.e. so that this would be a sign that they followed the Messenger and were patient in hardship while they were in a hard state.

zajjaj:135-135.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ يا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ﴾ — and ”مَكاناتِكم“ [is also read] — the meaning is: "act according to your ability (tamakkun)". And it is possible that the meaning is: "act according to what you are upon". One says to a man, when you command him to stay firm in a state: ”عَلى مَكانَتِكَ يا فُلانُ“ ("stay in your place, so-and-so"), that is: stay firm on what you are upon.

If someone says: How can it be permissible for the Prophet ﷺ to command them to persist in disbelief, saying to them "act according to your position"? The meaning of this command is only intensity in threatening, because by His saying to them ﴿فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَن تَكُونُ لَهُ عاقِبَةُ الدّارِ إنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾ He had made known to them that whoever does as they do, his destination is the Fire. So He said to them: "Persist in what you are upon, if you are content with the punishment of the Fire."

And ”اَلْحامِي“ is the [stallion] that has protected its back from being ridden. ﴿وَأنْعامٌ لا يَذْكُرُونَ اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها﴾ [al-Anʿām: 138]: so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that that is fabrication (iftirāʾ), that is: they do that as a fabrication against Him. It is accusative through His saying "they do not mention the name of Allah"; Sībawayh calls this "an object for which [the action is done]" (mafʿūl lahu, i.e. mafʿūl li-ajlihi — object of purpose). Its reality is that His saying "they do not mention" has the meaning of "they fabricate", so it is as though He said: "they fabricate a fabrication" (”يَفْتَرُونَ افْتِراءً“). «[Translator's note: so in the text; this last paragraph belongs to the commentary on verse 138 and appears here as transmitted.]»

zajjaj:139-139.t:
﴿وَقالُوا ما في بُطُونِ هَذِهِ الأنْعامِ خالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنا ومُحَرَّمٌ عَلى أزْواجِنا﴾: it seems that when they assigned to their idols something of what was in the bellies of the livestock, they made it whatever was born male and alive, to be eaten by the males exclusively, and they did not permit women to eat any of it; and if it was a dead male, men and women shared in it. That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنْ يَكُنْ مَيْتَةً فَهم فِيهِ شُرَكاءُ﴾.

Then He said: ﴿خالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنا﴾. It is of two kinds. The better of them is that He made the khabar (predicate) feminine, and gave ”ما“ a feminine meaning, because it is in the sense of a group; it is as though they said: "the whole of what is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males", and ”وَمُحَرَّمٌ“ is referred back to the wording of ”ما“. Some said: He made it feminine because of the femininity of "the livestock" (al-anʿām). [But] what is in the bellies of the livestock is not in the position of "part of a thing", because in your saying ”سَقَطَتْ بَعْضُ أصابِعِهِ“ ("some of his fingers fell off" — with the feminine verb), "some of [his] fingers" is a finger, and it is one of them; whereas what is in the bellies of the livestock — what is in the belly of each one — is other than it. And whoever said it is permissible on the basis that the whole is "livestock", it is as though he said: "and they said: the livestock that are in the bellies of the livestock are exclusively for our males". The first view, which we have explained, is clearer, because of His saying ”وَمُحَرَّمٌ“, since it is a proof of construing ”ما“ by meaning [and then] by wording. «[Translator's note: the final clause is garbled in the text (”دَلِيلٌ عَلى الحَمْلِ المَعْنى في ”ما“، عَلى اللَّفْظِ“); it is rendered by its evident sense.]»

Some read: ”خالِصَةً لِذُكُورِنا“ [in the accusative]; in my view — and Allah knows best — it is [in the sense of]: "what has come out pure, alive". ”وَإنْ يَكُنْ مَيْتَةً“ is permissible with yāʾ and with tāʾ, with the accusative of ”مَيْتَةً“; the meaning [with tāʾ] is: "and if those foetuses that are in the bellies are dead". Whoever reads ”وَإنْ يَكُنْ“ reads it according to the wording of ”ما“; the meaning is: "if what is in the belly is dead". And ”وَإنْ تَكُنْ مَيْتَةٌ“, with tāʾ and the nominative of ”مَيْتَةٌ“, is permissible, ”تَكُنْ“ then being in the sense of occurring and happening, as though it were "and if a dead one occurs" (”وَإنْ تَقَعْ مَيْتَةٌ“), and "if a dead one comes about" (”إنْ تَحْدُثْ مَيْتَةٌ“).

And His saying: ﴿سَيَجْزِيهِمْ وصْفَهُمْ﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: He will recompense them with the recompense of their description, which is a lie.

zajjaj:140-140.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَفَهًا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾: ”سَفَهًا“ is accusative in the sense of the lām, that is: "out of folly" (lil-safah), like ”فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ حَذَرَ الشَّرِّ“ ("I did that for fear of evil"). And it is possible that it is accusative on the interpretation of a maṣdar (verbal noun), because they acted foolishly in killing their children, so it is as though He said: "they acted foolishly a folly" (”سَفِهُوا سَفَهًا“). So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ قَتَلُوا أوْلادَهم سَفَهًا بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وحَرَّمُوا ما رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ افْتِراءً عَلى اللَّهِ﴾. We have already explained the accusative of ”اِفْتِراءً“; the meaning of iftirāʾ here is lying.

zajjaj:141-141.t:
Then Allah argued against them and drew attention to the enormity of what they had committed in daring to lie against Allah and daring to lay down as religion what Allah had not permitted. So He said: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أنْشَأ جَنّاتٍ مَعْرُوشاتٍ﴾, as though He said: "They fabricated against Allah, while He is the One who brings things into being, who does what no one is able to produce the like of." So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أنْشَأ﴾, that is: He originated trellised gardens. ”اَلْجَنّاتُ“ are orchards. ﴿وَغَيْرَ مَعْرُوشاتٍ﴾: the meaning of ”اَلْمَعْرُوشاتُ“ here is the vines. ﴿والنَّخْلَ والزَّرْعَ مُخْتَلِفًا أُكُلُهُ﴾: in the state of its produce being varied.

This is a difficult question in grammar, except for one who knows its reality, because someone may say: How did He produce it in the state of its produce being varied, when it grew before its produce came about — ”أُكُلُهُ“ being its fruit? The answer to that is that He, Mighty and Majestic is He, decreed its production by His saying: ﴿خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 102]; so He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He is the One who produces it in the state of its produce being varied. And it is permissible [to say] "He produced it when there was no produce in it, its produce being varied" (”أنْشَأهُ ولا أُكُلَ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفًا أُكُلُهُ“), because the meaning is "decreeing that in it" — as you say ”لَتَدْخُلُنَّ مَنزِلَ زَيْدٍ آكِلِينَ شارِبِينَ“ ("you shall surely enter Zayd's house eating and drinking"), the meaning being: "you enter intending that". Sībawayh pointed to that and explained it in his saying ”مَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلٍ مَعَهُ صَقْرٌ صائِدًا بِهِ غَدًا“ ("I passed by a man with a falcon, hunting with it tomorrow"): he put ”صائِدًا“ in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being "intending the hunt" [i.e. an anticipated ḥāl].

The meaning of ﴿مُتَشابِهًا وغَيْرَ مُتَشابِهٍ﴾ is of two kinds. One is that some of it resembles some, and some of it differs from some. And it may be that "alike and unlike" means that the fruits resemble one another in appearance and differ in tastes.

And His saying: ﴿كُلُوا مِن ثَمَرِهِ إذا أثْمَرَ﴾: ”ثَمَرٌ“ is the plural of ”ثَمَرَةٌ“. ”مِن ثُمُرِهِ“ is permissible, ”اَلثُّمُرُ“ being the plural of ”ثِمارٌ“, in the position of ”حُمُرٌ“, the plural of ”حِمارٌ“ (donkey). And ”مِن ثَمْرِهِ“, with sukūn on the mīm, is permissible.

And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآتُوا حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصادِهِ﴾: ”اَلْحَصادُ“ and ”اَلْحِصادُ“ (harvest) are both permissible, and it is read with both; like it are ”اَلْجَدادُ“ and ”اَلْجِدادُ“, for cutting the date-palms. People differed on the interpretation of ﴿وَآتُوا حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصادِهِ﴾. It is said that the verse is Meccan. It is related that Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās cut five hundred palms and distributed all their fruit, and brought none of it into his home; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿وَآتُوا حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصادِهِ ولا تُسْرِفُوا﴾. On this interpretation, when a person gives away all his wealth and lets none of it reach his dependants and family, he has been extravagant, because it has come in the report: "Begin with those you support." Others said: it is Medinan, and the meaning of "and give its due on the day of its harvest" is: pay what has been made obligatory upon you in its alms. There is no disagreement among the Muslims in the matter of zakāt that when fruits are harvested, it becomes obligatory to pay the alms due on them in what alms has been made obligatory. On this interpretation ”وَلا تُسْرِفُوا“ means: "do not spend your wealth and your alms in other than the direction that has been made obligatory upon you", as the idolaters said "this shall not be", and forbade what Allah had made lawful; and there is no extravagance clearer than spending wealth on what angers Allah.

zajjaj:142-142.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ الأنْعامِ حَمُولَةً وفَرْشًا﴾ is conjoined (nasaq) to "gardens"; the meaning is: "He is the One who produced gardens, and produced of the livestock beasts of burden and small ones." ”اَلْحَمُولَةُ“ are the camels that carry [loads], and the lexicographers are agreed that ”اَلْفَرْشُ“ are their small ones. Some of the exegetes said: ”اَلْفَرْشُ“ are the small camels, and the cattle and sheep are among the farsh mentioned in the exegesis; this is indicated by His saying: ﴿ثَمانِيَةَ أزْواجٍ مِنَ الضَّأْنِ اثْنَيْنِ ومِنَ المَعْزِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 143].

And His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ الإبِلِ اثْنَيْنِ ومِنَ البَقَرِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 144]: since this came as a badal (substitute) for His saying "beasts of burden and small ones", He made it include the cattle and the sheep along with the camels.

And His saying: ﴿كُلُوا مِمّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾, that is: "do not forbid what you have forbidden of what has been mentioned". ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُواتِ الشَّيْطانِ﴾: in ”خُطُواتِ“ there are three aspects: ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, fatḥa on it, and sukūn on it. The meaning of "the footsteps of Satan" is the paths of Satan. Some said: Satan's stepping over from the lawful to the forbidden. What the language indicates is that the meaning is: "do not travel the path that Satan makes attractive to you".

zajjaj:143-143.t: And His saying: ﴿ثَمانِيَةَ أزْواجٍ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for ”حَمُولَةً وفَرْشًا“. ”اَلزَّوْجُ“ in the language is the single one that has another with it. ﴿مِنَ الضَّأْنِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾: ”اَلضَّأْنُ“ is the plural of ”ضائِنٌ“; [one says] ”ضَأْنٌ“ like ”تاجِرٌ“ (merchant) and ”تَجْرٌ“. ﴿وَمِنَ المَعْزِ اثْنَيْنِ قُلْ آلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أمِ الأُنْثَيَيْنِ أمّا اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أرْحامُ الأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾: this is an argument against them, by which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, exposed their fabrication and their lying in what they claimed: that what is in the bellies of the livestock is lawful for the males and forbidden to the females, and the rest of what they forbade that we have described. So it was said to them: "Is it the two males He has forbidden?" If He had forbidden the males of the sheep, then all their males would be forbidden; if He had forbidden the two females, then all the females would be forbidden; and if He had forbidden what the wombs of the two females contain, then He would have forbidden the young — and all of them are young — so all of them would be forbidden. Likewise is the argument in His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ الإبِلِ اثْنَيْنِ ومِنَ البَقَرِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 144]. So it was said to them: ﴿نَبِّئُونِي بِعِلْمٍ﴾, that is: explain what you have forbidden with knowledge — that is, while you have no knowledge, because you do not believe in a Book.

zajjaj:144-144.t: ﴿أمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَداءَ إذْ وصّاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهَذا﴾, that is: "Did you witness Allah forbidding this, since you do not believe in a messenger?" Then He made their wrongdoing clear and said: ﴿فَمَن أظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا لِيُضِلَّ النّاسَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾. The argument has made clear that they do not believe in a prophet, and do not claim that a prophet informed them from Allah that this is forbidden, nor that they witnessed Allah forbidding it.

zajjaj:54-54.t:
And His words: ﴿وَإذا جاءَكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآياتِنا﴾, i.e. those who believe in Our arguments and Our proofs, ﴿فَقُلْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾. I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] mention that «السلام» in the language is four things. Among them: «سلّمت سلامًا», the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «سلّمت» ("I greeted"). Among them: «السلام» as the plural of «سلامة» (safety). Among them: «السلام» as one of the names of Allah the Exalted. And among them: «السلام» as a kind of tree; of it is his saying:
إلّا سَلامٌ وحَرْمَلُ
(… except salām trees and wild rue.)

The meaning of «السلام» which is the maṣdar of «سلّمت» is that it is a supplication for a person to be safe from afflictions in his religion and his self; its interpretation is "deliverance". «السلام» as one of the names of Allah — its interpretation, and Allah knows best, is: the Possessor of peace (salām), i.e. He is the One who owns salām, which is deliverance from what is disliked. As for «السلام» the tree, it is a large, strong tree; I reckon it was so named because of its being safe from afflictions. «السِّلام» are hard stones, so named because of their being free from softness. Peace-making is called «السِّلْم», «السَّلْم» and «السَّلَم», so named because its meaning is safety from evil. «السَّلْم» is a bucket with a single handle, like the water-carriers' bucket; the bucket was called «سَلْم» because it has fewer handles than other buckets, so it is the safest of them from defects. «السُّلَّم» is that on which one climbs (a ladder), so named because it delivers you safely to where you want; and «السُّلَّم» is the means to a thing, so named because it leads to something else, just as the ladder one climbs leads [up].

And His words: ﴿كَتَبَ رَبُّكم عَلى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ أنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ مِنكم سُوءًا بِجَهالَةٍ ثُمَّ تابَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وأصْلَحَ فَأنَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾: with fatḥa on both. It may also be «إنّه … فإنّه» with kasra on both; fatḥa on the first and kasra on the second is permissible; and kasra on the first and fatḥa on the second is permissible.

As for fatḥa on the first and the second, it is on the basis that the position of the first «أنّ» is accusative, the meaning being "your Lord has prescribed forgiveness for Himself", and it is a badal (substitute) for «الرحمة», as if He said: "Your Lord has prescribed mercy for Himself — namely forgiveness — for the repentant sinners", because the meaning of His being "forgiving, merciful" is forgiveness from Him. It is possible that the second came as a reinforcement (muʾakkida) of the first, because the meaning is "your Lord has prescribed that He is forgiving, merciful"; and when the speech grew long, the mention of «إنّ» was repeated.

As for kasra on both, it is on the way of ḥikāya (quotation), as if, when He said «كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة», He said: «إنّه من عمل منكم سوءًا بجهالة ثم تاب من بعده وأصلح فإنّه غفور رحيم», with kasra. The fāʾ is made the answer to the condition (jazāʾ), and «إنّ» has kasra since it has entered upon a mubtadaʾ and khabar, as if you said «فهو غفور رحيم» ("then He is forgiving, merciful"), except that the speech with «إنّ» is more emphatic.

Whoever puts kasra on the first does so on the basis of the ḥikāya we mentioned; and when he puts fatḥa on the second along with kasra on the first, it is because its meaning is the maṣdar and the khabar is omitted, the meaning being: "whoever does such-and-such, then Allah's forgiveness is his". Whoever puts fatḥa on the first and kasra on the second, the meaning goes back to the maṣdar, as though you had not mentioned the second «إنّ»; the meaning: "your Lord has prescribed for Himself that He is forgiving, merciful".

The meaning of «كتب» is: He made it binding with an emphatic obligation. It is also possible that He wrote that in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ); creation is addressed only with what they understand, and they understand that the confirmation of a deferred matter is preserved only by writing. We shall explain that in its place with a more thorough explanation than this, if Allah wills.

The meaning of ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ السُّوءَ بِجَهالَةٍ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 17] is not that they are ignorant that it is evil; if a Muslim did something not knowing that it was evil, he would be like one who did not intend evil and did not commit evil. Your saying «عمل فلان كذا وكذا بجهالة» ("so-and-so did such-and-such in ignorance") admits two things. One of them is that he did it while ignorant of the harm in it, i.e. he did not know that there was harm in it. The other: he undertook it with full awareness, knowing that its outcome would be harmful, but preferred the immediate, and so he was deemed ignorant, for he preferred a little over abundant ease and lasting well-being. This is the meaning of «من عمل منكم سوءًا بجهالة».

zajjaj:55-55.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الآياتِ ولِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ المُجْرِمِينَ﴾ is read with the tāʾ and with the yāʾ. Whoever reads with the tāʾ does so because «السبيل» is the road, and it is treated as masculine and feminine. A third possibility is permissible: «ولتستبينَ سبيلَ المجرمين», with «السبيل» in the accusative, because the meaning is "and that you, O Muḥammad, may discern the way of the criminals".
[Translator's note: the author gives the reason only for the reading with the tāʾ; the yāʾ reading (masculine «سبيل») is not explained separately.]

If someone says: "Was the Prophet ﷺ not already discerning the way of the criminals?", the answer to this is that everything with which the believers are addressed, the Prophet ﷺ is addressed with; so it is as if He said «ولتستبينوا سبيل المجرمين» ("and that you [all] may discern the way of the criminals"), i.e. that you may increase in discerning it.

He did not need to say «ولتستبين سبيلُ المؤمنين» ("and that the way of the believers may become clear") along with mentioning the way of the criminals, because when the way of the criminals becomes clear, the way of the believers has become clear along with it. It is possible that the meaning is: "that the way of the criminals may become clear and that the way of the believers may become clear", except that the mention and the address here concern the criminals, so they were mentioned, and mention of the way of the believers was left out because there is an indication of it in the speech — just as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 81] and did not say "protecting you from cold", because a covering protects from heat and cold; but heat was mentioned because in their land they suffered from it more than from cold.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
And His words: ﴿قُلْ إنِّي نُهِيتُ أنْ أعْبُدَ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾: they used to worship idols and said: "We worship them only so that they may bring us near to Allah". So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that none but He is to be worshipped.

And His words: ﴿قُلْ لا أتَّبِعُ أهْواءَكُمْ﴾, i.e. you have worshipped them only by way of whim, not by way of clear evidence and proof.

And His words: ﴿قَدْ ضَلَلْتُ إذًا﴾: the meaning of «إذن» is the meaning of a condition (sharṭ); the meaning: "I would have gone astray if I worshipped them".

And His words: ﴿وَما أنا مِنَ المُهْتَدِينَ﴾, i.e. and I would not be among the prophets who travelled the path of guidance.

zajjaj:57-57.t:
And His words: ﴿قُلْ إنِّي عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِن رَبِّي﴾, i.e. upon a clear matter, not a follower of whim. ﴿وَكَذَّبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾: this hāʾ is a pronoun (kināya) referring to the clarification (al-bayān), i.e. and you denied the clarification, because «البيّنة» and «البيان» have one meaning. Or «وكذبتم به» means: what I have brought you, because that is the clarification.

And His words: ﴿ما عِنْدِي ما تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِهِ﴾: what they sought to hasten were the signs which they proposed to him; so he ﷺ made known that that is with Allah, and said: «إن الحكم إلا لله يقض الحق وهو خير الفاصلين». This was written here without the yāʾ according to the pronunciation, because the yāʾ was dropped on account of the meeting of two quiescent letters, just as they wrote ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبانِيَةَ﴾ [al-ʿAlaq: 18] without the wāw.

It has been read «يقصُّ الحق», and Ibn ʿAbbās read «يقضي بالحق», except that the readers do not read «يقضي بالحق» because it contradicts the codex (muṣḥaf). «يقضي الحق» has two aspects: «الحقّ» may be an adjective of the maṣdar, the meaning being "He decrees the true decree"; or «يقضي الحق» may mean "He makes the truth", i.e. everything He, Mighty and Majestic, makes is truth and wisdom — except that ﴿وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الفاصِلِينَ﴾ points to the meaning of «القضاء» which is judgement. As for «قضى» in the meaning of «صنع» (to make), its like is the saying of al-Hudhalī:
؎وَعَلَيْهِما مَسْرُودَتانِ قَضاهُما ∗∗∗ داوُدُ أوْ صَنَعَ السَّوابِغَ تُبَّعُ
(Upon the two of them were two coats of linked mail which Dāwūd had wrought, or Tubbaʿ, maker of full-length mail.)
i.e. Dāwūd made them. Whoever reads «يقص الحق», its meaning is that everything He has told of and commanded is among the true narratives.

zajjaj:59-59.t:
And His words: ﴿وَعِنْدَهُ مَفاتِحُ الغَيْبِ لا يَعْلَمُها إلا هُوَ﴾: the meaning of «مفاتح الغيب» is: with Him is the means of access to knowledge of the unseen; and of everything that is not known, when knowledge of it is sought, one says «افتح عليّ» ("open it to me"). His words: ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ ما في البَرِّ والبَحْرِ وما تَسْقُطُ مِن ورَقَةٍ إلا يَعْلَمُها﴾: the meaning is that He knows it falling and fixed [on the tree]; you say «ما يجيئك أحد إلا وأنا أعرفه» ("no one comes to you but I know him"), and its meaning is not "but I know him only at the time of his coming".

«ولا حبّةٍ» is permissible, and «ولا حبّةٌ» is permissible. Whoever puts it in the nominative does so on two grounds: it may be on the meaning «ما تسقط ورقةٌ ولا حبّةٌ في ظلمات الأرض ولا رطبٌ ولا يابسٌ إلا في كتاب مبين» ("no leaf falls, nor grain in the darkness of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear book"). «في كتاب مبين» here varies between two meanings: the meaning of «في كتاب مبين» may be that Allah recorded that in a book before it was created, as He said: ﴿ما أصابَ مِن مُصِيبَةٍ في الأرْضِ ولا في أنْفُسِكم إلا في كِتابٍ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ نَبْرَأها﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 22]; so He made known that He had recorded what He created before He created it.
[Translator's note: the author announces two grounds for the nominative and two meanings of «في كتاب مبين», but the text as it stands gives only the first of each.]

zajjaj:145-145.t:
Then He said: ﴿قُلْ لا أجِدُ في ما أُوحِيَ إلَيَّ مُحَرَّمًا﴾. So he ﷺ made known to them that forbidding and permitting are accepted only through revelation or the sent-down [Book]. So He said: ﴿قُلْ لا أجِدُ في ما أُوحِيَ إلَيَّ مُحَرَّمًا عَلى طاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ إلا أنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أوْ دَمًا مَسْفُوحًا﴾. ”اَلْمَسْفُوحُ“ is what is poured out; it seems that when they slaughtered they would eat the blood just as they ate the meat. ﴿أوْ لَحْمَ خِنْـزِيرٍ﴾, for it is rijs; ”اَلرِّجْسُ“ is a name for what is regarded as filthy, and for punishment. ﴿أوْ فِسْقًا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ﴾, that is: the voice was raised over its slaughter with the name of other than Allah; they used to mention the names of their idols over their slaughtered animals. So ”فِسْقًا“ is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to ”لَحْمَ خِنْزِيرٍ“; the meaning is: "unless what is eaten is carrion, or blood poured out, or the flesh of swine, or a transgression". So what has had other than the name of Allah mentioned over it is called "fisq", that is: a going out from the religion. ﴿فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ باغٍ﴾, that is: necessity drove him to eat it, so he ate it not desiring, that is: not intending to make lawful what Allah has forbidden. ﴿وَلا عادٍ﴾, that is: nor exceeding moderation and the measure of need; ”اَلْعادِي“ is the wrongdoer. ﴿فَإنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, that is: He forgives whoever does not transgress.

As for the i'rab of ”آلذَّكَرَيْنِ“, it is accusative by ”حَرَّمَ“. The alif of the definite article is retained along with the alif of interrogation so that the interrogative is not confused with the declarative; for if it were said ”ألذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ“ with a single alif, the interrogative would be confused with the declarative. With ”أمْ“, dropping the alif may be permissible, because ”أمْ“ indicates the interrogative: if it were said ”ألرَّجُلَ ضَرَبْتَ أمِ الغُلامَ“ ("did you strike the man or the boy?"), ”أمْ“ would indicate that the first is included in the interrogation. Sībawayh permitted the verse to be on this basis, namely his saying:
؎لَعَمْرُكَ ما أدْرِي وإنْ كُنْتُ دارِيًا ∗∗∗ شُعَيْثُ بْنُ سَهْمٍ أمْ شُعْيْثُ بْنُ مِنقَرِ
(By your life, I do not know — though I am one who knows — whether Shuʿayth are [sons] of Sahm or Shuʿayth of Minqar.)
So he permitted it to be on [the reading] ”أشُعَيْثُ بْنُ سَهْمٍ؟“. But the reading is with the second alif made clear in His saying ”آلذَّكَرَيْنِ“.

zajjaj:146-146.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَعَلى الَّذِينَ هادُوا حَرَّمْنا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ﴾: by it are meant camels and ostriches, because ostriches have claws (ẓufur), like camels. ﴿وَمِنَ البَقَرِ والغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُما إلا ما حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُما﴾: some people said: The omenta (al-thurūb) were forbidden to them, and lawful to them was what else there was of what the backs carry, ﴿أوِ الحَوايا﴾ — that is, the intestines (al-mabāʿir), whose singular is ”حاوِيَةٌ“, ”حاوِياءُ“ and ”حَوِيَّةٌ“ — ﴿أوْ ما اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ﴾, such as the fat of the rump. This is the more widely held of the two views. Others said: the omenta were forbidden to them, and what the backs carry was made lawful to them; and the intestines, or what is mixed with bone, became [forbidden], except what the backs carry, for that is not forbidden. «[Translator's note: the second view is compressed in the text; the word "forbidden" is supplied from the context.]»

”أوْ“ has entered in the way of permission (ibāḥa), as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَلا تُطِعْ مِنهم آثِمًا أوْ كَفُورًا﴾ [al-Insān: 24]; the meaning is: "all of these deserve to be disobeyed, so disobey this one and disobey that one". ”أوْ“ is eloquent in this meaning, because if you say ”لا تُطِعْ زَيْدًا وعَمْرًا“ ("do not obey Zayd and ʿAmr"), it is possible that you have forbidden me to obey the two of them together, in which case, if I obeyed Zayd alone, I would not have disobeyed you. But if you say ”لا تُطِعْ زَيْدًا أوْ عَمْرًا أوْ خالِدًا“ ("do not obey Zayd or ʿAmr or Khālid"), the meaning is that all of these deserve not to be obeyed, so do not obey any one of them, and do not obey the group. Like it is ”جالِسِ الحَسَنَ أوِ ابْنَ سِيرِينَ أوِ الشَّعْبِيَّ“ ("sit with al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn or al-Shaʿbī"): the meaning is not that I command you to sit with one of them; rather the meaning of ”أوْ“ is permission. The meaning is: all of them deserve to be sat with; if you sit with one of them you are right, and if you sit with the group you are right.

zajjaj:148-148.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ أشْرَكُوا لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما أشْرَكْنا ولا آباؤُنا﴾: Sībawayh claimed that conjoining an overt noun to a nominative pronoun that is not expressed separately (al-muḍmar al-marfūʿ) is ugly: ”قُمْتَ وزَيْدٌ“ ("you stood, and Zayd") and ”قامَ وزَيْدٌ“ are deemed ugly; but if ”لا“ comes, the speech becomes good, and you say ”لا قُمْتَ ولا زَيْدٌ“, just as when one adds tawkīd (emphasis) and says ”قُمْتَ أنْتَ وزَيْدٌ“, it is good. It is permissible in poetry.

As for the meaning of the verse: Allah, exalted is His praise, informed about them of what they would say. Their saying ﴿لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما أشْرَكْنا﴾ — they made this saying an argument for persisting in their associating of partners. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that ﴿كَذَلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ حَتّى ذاقُوا بَأْسَنا﴾. The argument against them in this is that if they believe that everyone who is upon something — things proceeding by the will of Allah the Exalted — is in the right, then, according to their saying, there is no point to the message and the prophets. So it is said to them: Those who are upon a religion contrary to yours — are they not upon what Allah has willed? Then you ought not to say that they are astray. He, Mighty and Majestic is He, does what He wills; He is able to guide all creatures, and the servants have no claim against Allah that He should do with them everything He is able to do. So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الحُجَّةُ البالِغَةُ فَلَوْ شاءَ لَهَداكم أجْمَعِينَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 149]. His conclusive argument is His making clear that He is the One, and His sending the prophets with proofs that the created are unable to produce.

zajjaj:150-150.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ هَلُمَّ شُهَداءَكُمُ﴾: Sībawayh claimed that it is ”ها“ to which ”لُمَّ“ has been joined, and the two have been made like a single word. The most common usage is to say ”هَلُمَّ“ for one, two and a group; the Quran came with that, as in their saying: ﴿هَلُمَّ إلَيْنا﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 18]. The meaning of ﴿هَلُمَّ شُهَداءَكُمُ﴾ is: bring your witnesses, and bring your witnesses near. Among the Arabs are those who make it dual, plural and feminine, saying to a male ”هَلُمَّ“, to two ”هَلُمّا“, to a group ”هَلُمُّوا“, to a woman ”هَلُمِّي“, to two women ”هَلُمّا“, and to women ”هَلْمُمْنَ“. The mīm takes fatḥa because it is assimilated (mudgham), just as ”رُدَّ“ takes fatḥa in the imperative, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ”هَلُمُّ إلَيْنا“ with ḍamma is not permissible for one person, as fatḥa, ḍamma and kasra are permissible in ”رُدَّ“, because it [هَلُمَّ] is not inflected (lā tataṣarraf).

zajjaj:151-151.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ تَعالَوْا أتْلُ ما حَرَّمَ رَبُّكم عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: ”ما“ is in the position of an accusative — if you wish, by ”أتْلُ“, the meaning being: "Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you". And it is possible that ”ما“ is accusative by ”حَرَّمَ“, because reciting is in the position of saying; it is as though He said: "I say: what has your Lord forbidden you? This, or this?" It is possible that what he recited to them is His saying: ﴿إلا أنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أوْ دَمًا مَسْفُوحًا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 145], and that ”ألّا تُشْرِكُوا“ is accusative in the sense of the dropping of the lām, that is: I make clear to you what is forbidden so that you do not associate anything with Him — because when they forbid what Allah has made lawful, they have made other than Allah, in accepting from him, in the position of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, and by that they become associators. And it is possible that ”ألّا تُشْرِكُوا“ is construed by meaning, so that it is "I recite to you that you should not associate anything with Him", the meaning being: "I recite to you the prohibition of associating [anything] with Him". And it is possible that it is in the sense of "I enjoin you not to associate anything with Him", because His saying ﴿وَبِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا﴾ is construed in the sense of "I enjoin you to [show] kindness to parents".

And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أوْلادَكم مِن إمْلاقٍ﴾, that is: do not kill your children out of poverty, that is: out of fear of poverty. ﴿وَلا تَقْرَبُوا الفَواحِشَ ما ظَهَرَ مِنها وما بَطَنَ﴾: [”ما ظَهَرَ“] is a badal (substitute) for ”اَلْفَواحِشَ“, in the position of an accusative; the meaning is: "do not approach what is open of indecencies and what is hidden". It has come in the exegesis that what is hidden of them is fornication, and what is open is taking lovers and companions in a suspect manner. «[Translator's note: so in the text; under 6:120 the same report is given the other way round (open = fornication, hidden = taking lovers).]» The apparent sense of the speech is that what has been mentioned — associating partners with Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, killing children, and all that they forbade of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made lawful — are indecencies; so He said: "Do not approach these indecencies, whether openly or secretly." And Allah knows best.

And His saying: ﴿ذَلِكم وصّاكم بِهِ﴾ indicates the meaning of ﴿ألا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا وبِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا﴾.

zajjaj:152-152.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْرَبُوا مالَ اليَتِيمِ إلا بِالَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ﴾: some said: "that which is best" is riding his mount and making use of his servant. But there is nothing in the apparent sense to show that this is what is intended; "that which is best" is only guarding his property for him and making it grow by whatever means are found. His saying: ﴿حَتّى يَبْلُغَ أشُدَّهُ﴾: ”حَتّى“ is construed by meaning; the meaning is: guard it for him until he reaches his maturity, that is: when he reaches his maturity, hand it over to him. Reaching his maturity is that sound judgement (rushd) is perceived in him, together with his being of age. Some said: "until he reaches his maturity" means until he reaches eighteen years. I do not know what the basis of that is, since if he comes of age before eighteen and sound judgement has been perceived in him, handing his property over to him is obligatory.

And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإذا قُلْتُمْ فاعْدِلُوا ولَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى﴾, that is: when you testify or judge, be just, even if the one testified against, or for, is a relative.

zajjaj:154-154.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ تَمامًا عَلى الَّذِي أحْسَنَ﴾: most readers read it with fatḥa on the nūn. ”أحْسَنُ“ [with ḍamma] is permissible, implying "upon that which is best" (”عَلى الَّذِي هو أحْسَنُ“). As for the fatḥa, it is on the basis that ”أحْسَنَ“ is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa. The Kufans permitted it to be in the position of a genitive and to be an adjective (ṣifa) of ”اَلَّذِي“; in the view of the Basrans this is a gross error. The Basrans claimed that they know ”اَلَّذِي“ only as a relative noun (mawṣūla) and that it is not qualified until its ṣila (relative clause) is complete, and the Kufans agreed with them that the proper way is [for it to have] its ṣila; so they [the Kufans] would need to establish that it has been raised [i.e. used] as a relative noun with no ṣila.

As for the entry of ”ثُمَّ“ in His saying ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنا﴾ — when we know that what comes after ”ثُمَّ“ can never mean what is prior, and we know that the Quran was sent down after Mūsā and after the Torah, yet He said ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ﴾ — ”ثُمَّ“ entered only in conjunction with the reciting, and the meaning is: "Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you; I recite to you that you should not kill your children, and do not kill the soul that Allah has forbidden; then I recite what Allah gave Mūsā."

The meaning of ”عَلى الَّذِي أحْسَنَ“ may be "complete upon the one who does good" (”تَمامًا عَلى المُحْسِنِ“), the meaning being "a completion from Allah upon those who do good". And "complete upon that which he did well" may mean: "upon the obedience to Allah and following His command that Mūsā did well". And "complete upon that which is the best of things" (”تَمامًا عَلى الَّذِي هو أحْسَنُ الأشْياءِ“) is permissible. ”تَمامًا“ is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and likewise ﴿وَتَفْصِيلا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾; the meaning is: "We gave it to him for this reason", that is, for completion and detailed explanation.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفّاكم بِاللَّيْلِ﴾, i.e. He makes you sleep, and so takes your souls by which you discern, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿اللَّهُ يَتَوَفّى الأنْفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِها والَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ في مَنامِها﴾ [al-Zumar: 42]. The meaning of ﴿يَبْعَثُكم فِيهِ﴾ is: He wakes you from your sleep in it, in the daytime. ﴿لِيُقْضى أجَلٌ مُسَمًّى﴾, i.e. He raises you from your sleep until you reach your appointed terms.

zajjaj:61-61.t:
And His words: ﴿وَهُوَ القاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبادِهِ ويُرْسِلُ عَلَيْكم حَفَظَةً﴾: «الحفظة» (the guardians) are the angels; the singular is «حافظ» and the plural «حفظة», like «كاتب» and «كتبة», [i.e. the pattern] «فاعل» and «فعلة».

And His words: ﴿حَتّى إذا جاءَ أحَدَكُمُ المَوْتُ تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنا﴾, i.e. these guardians, because He said: ﴿وَيُرْسِلُ عَلَيْكم حَفَظَةً﴾. ﴿وَهم لا يُفَرِّطُونَ﴾, i.e. they are not heedless and do not slacken. The meaning of «التفريط» in the language is putting forward incapacity; so the meaning is that they do not fall short.

zajjaj:63-63.t:
And His words: ﴿قُلْ مَن يُنَجِّيكم مِن ظُلُماتِ البَرِّ والبَحْرِ﴾: in reading, «يُنْجِيكم» without doubling (takhfīf) is permissible, because of His words ﴿لَئِنْ أنْجَيْتَنا﴾ [Yūnus: 22] and ﴿لَئِنْ أنْجانا﴾; but the better is «يُنَجِّيكم» with doubling (tashdīd), for multiplicity. The meaning of «ظلمات البر والبحر» is "the hardships of land and sea". The Arabs say of a day in which they meet hardship «يوم مظلم» ("a dark day"), to the extent that they say «يوم ذو كواكب» ("a day with stars"), i.e. its darkness has become so intense that it has become like night. The poet said:
؎بَنِي أسَدٍ هَلْ تَعْلَمُونَ بَلاءَنا ∗∗∗ إذا كانَ يَوْمٌ ذُو كَواكِبَ أشْهَبُ
(O Banū Asad, do you know our valour, when there comes a grey day in which the stars appear?)
And they recited:
؎فِدًى لَبَنِي ذُهْلِ بْنِ شَيْبانَ ناقَتِي ∗∗∗ إذا كانَ يَوْمًا ذا كَواكِبَ أشْنَعا
(My she-camel is a ransom for the Banū Dhuhl ibn Shaybān, when it is a hideous day in which the stars appear.)
So the meaning of «ظلمات البر والبحر» is: their hardships.

And His words: ﴿تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعًا وخُفْيَةً﴾, with ḍamma and kasra in «خفية». The meaning is: you call upon Him displaying ḍarāʿa — which is intense need of a thing and want — and «تدعونه خفية», i.e. you call upon Him within yourselves, concealing in your poverty and your needs of Him, as you conceal.
[Translator's note: the final phrase «كما تضمرون» ("as you conceal") is as printed and appears incomplete.]

And His words: ﴿لَئِنْ أنْجانا مِن هَذِهِ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الشّاكِرِينَ﴾, i.e. in whatever hardship you fell into you said: "If He saves us from this, we shall surely be among the grateful". So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded that he ask them by way of rebuke to them and of making them acknowledge that it is He who saves them.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
Then they associate with Him the idols which they know to be of their own making, and which neither benefit nor harm, while [they know] that He is able to punish them. So He said: ﴿قُلْ هو القادِرُ عَلى أنْ يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكم عَذابًا مِن فَوْقِكُمْ﴾, like the stones which He rained upon the people of Lūṭ, and like the flood by which the people of Pharaoh were drowned; ﴿أوْ مِن تَحْتِ أرْجُلِكُمْ﴾, like the swallowing up by the earth which befell Qārūn and those swallowed up; ﴿أوْ يَلْبِسَكم شِيَعًا﴾: the meaning of «يلبسكم» is: He confounds your affair with a confusion of disorder, not a mixing of agreement. One says «لبَستُ الأمرَ ألبِسُه» — I did not make it clear and mixed parts of it with others; and one says «لبِستُ الثوبَ ألبَسُه» ("I put on the garment"). The meaning of «شيعًا» is: He makes you into factions, so you are not one faction; and when you are at variance, some of you fight others, which is the meaning of His words: ﴿وَيُذِيقَ بَعْضَكم بَأْسَ بَعْضٍ﴾.

It is related that the Prophet ﷺ asked Allah, Majestic and Mighty, not to afflict this community with a punishment by which He would uproot it, and not to make some of it taste the violence of others; so He answered him concerning averting the punishment, but did not answer him concerning not making some of it taste the violence of others and that it should not differ.

zajjaj:66-66.t: ﴿وَكَذَّبَ بِهِ قَوْمُكَ وهو الحَقُّ قُلْ لَسْتُ عَلَيْكم بِوَكِيلٍ﴾, i.e. I only call you to Allah and to His law; I have not been commanded to make war on you, nor to hold you to faith in the way one entrusted with a thing is held to carry it through to its end.

zajjaj:67-67.t: His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لِكُلِّ نَبَإٍ مُسْتَقَرٌّ﴾, i.e. for holding you to faith by way of war, compelling you to it and fighting you over it, there is a fixed term (mustaqarr), i.e. a time. ﴿وَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾: it may be that He threatened them with the punishment of the Hereafter, and it may be that He threatened them with war and holding them to faith whether they wished or refused — unless the People of the Book pay the jizya.

zajjaj:69-69.t: And His words: ﴿وَما عَلى الَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ مِن حِسابِهِمْ مِن شَيْءٍ ولَكِنْ ذِكْرى﴾, i.e. there is nothing upon you, O Prophet, nor upon the believers, of their reckoning, i.e. of their disbelief and their opposing Allah's command. «ولكن ذكرى», i.e. but it is upon you to remind them. «ذكرى» may be in the position of the nominative or the accusative. Whoever takes it as accusative, the meaning is «ولكن ذكّروهم ذكرى» ("but remind them with a reminding"). Whoever takes it as nominative does so on two aspects: one of them is «ولكن عليكم أن تذكروهم» ("but upon you is to remind them"), as He said: ﴿إنْ عَلَيْكَ إلا البَلاغُ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 48]; and it may be «ولكن الذي تأمرون به ذكرى» ("but what you are commanded with is a reminder"). ﴿لَعَلَّهم يَتَّقُونَ﴾, i.e. so that godfearingness may be hoped for from them.

zajjaj:70-70.t:
And His words: ﴿وَذَكِّرْ بِهِ أنْ تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ بِما كَسَبَتْ﴾: the meaning of «تُبسَل بعملها» is that it becomes unable to free itself. «المستبسل» is the one who surrenders, who knows that he cannot free himself. The poet said:
؎وَإبْسالِي بَنِيَّ بِغَيْرِ جُرْمٍ ∗∗∗ بَعَوْناهُ ولا بِدَمٍ مُراقِ
(And my surrendering my sons, for no crime we committed and for no blood shed.)
i.e. my handing them over. It has been said that «أن تبسل» means "be held in pledge", and the meaning is the same. One says «أسد باسل» ("a fierce lion") and «شجاع باسل» ("a fierce warrior"); its interpretation is that he has such boldness that his adversary gives himself up to him. One says «هذا بَسْلٌ عليك», i.e. forbidden to you; so «أسد باسل» may be from this, i.e. one who cannot be overcome. One says «أعطِ الرّافيَ بَسْلَتَه» ("give the charmer his fee"), i.e. his wage; its interpretation is that he has done the thing for which its owner gave himself up to him.
[Translator's note: the printed text has «الرّافِيَ»; this is most likely «الرّاقي» (the one who recites charms), the usual wording of this expression. The Arabic is kept as printed; the English follows «الراقي».]

zajjaj:71-71.t:
And His words: ﴿وَنُرَدُّ عَلى أعْقابِنا بَعْدَ إذْ هَدانا اللَّهُ﴾, i.e. we return to disbelief. Of everyone who turns back one says «قد رجع إلى خلف» ("he has gone back") and «رجع القهقرى» ("he has retreated backwards").

And His words: ﴿كالَّذِي اسْتَهْوَتْهُ الشَّياطِينُ في الأرْضِ﴾, i.e. like the one for whom the devils have made his whim seem fair.

And His words: ﴿حَيْرانَ﴾: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. like the one whom they have lured while in a state of bewilderment.

And His words: ﴿لَهُ أصْحابٌ يَدْعُونَهُ إلى الهُدى﴾: it is said in the exegesis that this refers to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr. ﴿ائْتِنا﴾, i.e. follow us in our faith. ﴿وَأُمِرْنا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾, i.e. they call him and say to him: "We have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds".

The Arabs say «أمرتك بأن تفعل», «أمرتك لتفعل» and «أمرتك أن تفعل» ("I commanded you to do"). Whoever says «أمرتك بأن تفعل», the bāʾ is for attachment (ilṣāq), the meaning being: the command fell upon this act. Whoever says «أمرتك أن تفعل» does so with the omission of the bāʾ. And whoever says «أمرتك لتفعل» has stated the reason for which the command took place; the meaning: "we have been commanded for [the sake of] Islam".

zajjaj:72-72.t: His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَأنْ أقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾: there are two aspects in it. One of them is that it is «أُمرنا لأن نسلم ولأن نقيم الصلاة» ("we have been commanded to submit and to establish the prayer"). And it may be construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is «أُمرنا بالإسلام وبإقامة الصلاة» ("we have been commanded with Islam and with establishing the prayer"); the position of «أن» is accusative, because when the bāʾ dropped, the verb reached [it directly] and so it became accusative. There is another aspect in it: it may be construed upon His words «يدعونه إلى الهدى ائتنا وأن أقيموا الصلاة», i.e. and they call him [saying] «أن أقيموا الصلاة» ("establish the prayer").

zajjaj:155-155.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَهَذا كِتابٌ أنْـزَلْناهُ مُبارَكٌ﴾: ”اَلْمُبارَكُ“ (the blessed) is that from which much good comes. It is a naʿt (adjective) of ”كِتابٌ“. As for whoever reads ”أنْزَلْناهُ مُبارَكًا“ [in the accusative], that is permissible outside the [canonical] reading, because the muṣḥaf may not be contradicted at all.

And His saying: ﴿فاتَّبِعُوهُ واتَّقُوا لَعَلَّكم تُرْحَمُونَ﴾, that is: so that you may be hoping for mercy.

zajjaj:156-156.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أنْ تَقُولُوا إنَّما أُنْـزِلَ الكِتابُ عَلى طائِفَتَيْنِ مِن قَبْلِنا﴾: some said its meaning is: We sent it down lest you say: "The Book was only sent down…", that is: We sent it down so that their argument would be cut off — even though the argument already belonged to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, because the Books that were sent down before the Prophet ﷺ contained the argument, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, would not leave His creation neglected without an argument; but in the sending down of the Book and [the sending of] the Prophet ﷺ there is the utmost of argument and an increase in clarification.

The Basrans said: its meaning is "We sent it down out of dislike that you should say", and they do not permit an implied ”لا“: they do not say ”جِئْتُ أنْ أُكْرِمَكَ“ ("I came that I honour you") meaning "lest I honour you"; but ”فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ أنْ أُكْرِمَكَ“ ("I did that that I honour you") is permissible, implying "out of love that I honour you" (”مَحَبَّةَ أنْ أُكْرِمَكَ“) or "out of dislike that I honour you" (”كَراهَةَ أنْ أُكْرِمَكَ“), the situation making known what is implied. So the meaning is: "He sent down the Book out of dislike that they should say: The Books were only sent down to the followers of Mūsā and ʿĪsā." ﴿وَإنْ كُنّا عَنْ دِراسَتِهِمْ لَغافِلِينَ﴾: the meaning is: "and we were nothing but unaware of the recitation of their Books".

zajjaj:157-157.t:
﴿أوْ تَقُولُوا﴾: the meaning is: "or out of dislike that you should say: ﴿لَوْ أنّا أُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْنا الكِتابُ لَكُنّا أهْدى مِنهُمْ﴾". They would only say "we would have been better guided than they" because they prided themselves on [sharp] minds and good understanding; that is because they memorised their poems, their reports and their traditions, while being unlettered people who did not write.

And His saying: ﴿فَقَدْ جاءَكم بَيِّنَةٌ مِن رَبِّكم وهُدًى ورَحْمَةٌ﴾, that is: there has come to you that in which there is clear explanation and the cutting off of doubts from you.

zajjaj:158-158.t:
And His saying: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا أنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ﴾, that is: "except that the angels of death come to them". ﴿أوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ﴾: or that your Lord's destruction of them and His vengeance on them come, either by a hastened punishment or by the Resurrection. This is like our saying ”قَدْ نَزَلَ فُلانٌ بِبَلَدِ كَذا وكَذا“ ("so-and-so has descended upon such-and-such a land") and ”قَدْ أتاهم فُلانٌ“ ("so-and-so has come upon them"), that is: he has fallen upon them.

And His saying: ﴿أوْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْضُ آياتِ رَبِّكَ﴾, such as the emergence of the Beast, or the rising of the sun from its place of setting.

And His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتِي بَعْضُ آياتِ رَبِّكَ لا يَنْفَعُ نَفْسًا إيمانُها لَمْ تَكُنْ آمَنَتْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾, that is: faith will not benefit it at the sign that compels you to believe, because Allah, exalted is His praise, has said: ”إنَّما تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ“ ("you are only recompensed for what you used to do"), and He sent the messengers with signs that are to be reflected upon, so that the one who believes in them has a reward. Had Allah sent punishment upon everyone who did not believe, people would have been compelled to believe in Him, and moral obligation (taklīf) and recompense would have fallen away.

zajjaj:159-159.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهم وكانُوا شِيَعًا لَسْتَ مِنهم في شَيْءٍ﴾: some said this was revealed before warfare, that is: fighting them is not your duty; their affair rests only with Allah. The meaning of "and they became sects" is: they were divided in their religion. By it are meant the Jews and the Christians, because the Christians declare one another disbelievers, and likewise the Jews; and they too [the Christians] are people of the Torah, and they declare one another disbelievers — I mean, the Jews declare the Christians disbelievers and the Christians declare the Jews disbelievers. In this verse there is an urging that the word of the Muslims be one, that they not split in religion, and that they not invent innovations as far as they are able. So His saying ﴿لَسْتَ مِنهم في شَيْءٍ﴾ indicates that whoever of the people of the religion of Islam splits his religion and invents innovations has thereby become one of them.

The meaning of ”شَيَّعْتُ“ in the language is "I followed". The Arabs say ”شاعَكُمُ السِّلْمُ“ and ”أشاعَكُمُ السَّلْمُ“, meaning "peace has followed you". The poet said:
؎ألا يا نَخْلَةً مِن ذاتِ عِرْقٍ ∗∗∗ بَرُودَ الظِّلِّ شايَعَكِ الظَّلامُ
(O palm tree of Dhāt ʿIrq, cool of shade, may the darkness accompany you.)
And you say ”آتِيكَ غَدًا، أوْ شِيَعَهُ“ ("I will come to you tomorrow, or the day after it"), that is: or the day that follows it. So the meaning of ”اَلشِّيعَةُ“ is those some of whom follow others, and the meaning of ”اَلشِّيَعُ“ is the factions, each faction of which has its members following one another, while they are not all in agreement.

zajjaj:160-160.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَن جاءَ بِالحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أمْثالِها﴾: the reading is ”فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أمْثالِها“, and the meaning is: "he will have ten good deeds like it" (”فَلَهُ عَشْرُ حَسَناتٍ أمْثالِها“), just as ”عِنْدِي خَمْسَةٌ أثْوابًا“ ("I have five, garments") is permissible. ”فَلَهُ عَشْرُ مِثْلِها“ is permissible outside the reading, ”اَلْمِثْلُ“ then being singular in wording and plural in meaning, as He said: ”إنَّكم إذًا مِّثْلُهم“ ("you would then be like them"). Whoever says ”أمْثالِها“, it is like His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لا يَكُونُوا أمْثالَكُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 38]. The singular came on mithl, while being in the meaning of the plural, only because it is according to the measure of what it is likened to; you say ”مَرَرْتُ بِقَوْمٍ مِثْلِكم“ and ”بِقَوْمٍ أمْثالِكم“ ("I passed by a people like you").

As for the meaning of the verse, it is among the subtle meanings in the view of the lexicographers, because the recompense from Allah, exalted is His praise, for a good deed — by entry into Paradise — is something whose measure cannot be described. So when He says "ten like it", or says ﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أمْوالَهم في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنابِلَ في كُلِّ سُنْبُلَةٍ مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ﴾ [al-Baqara: 261], together with His saying ﴿مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ أضْعافًا كَثِيرَةً﴾ [al-Baqara: 245], the meaning of all this is that the recompense of Allah, exalted is His praise, for good deeds is by multiplication of the single like, which is the utmost of estimation in [people's] souls; and Allah multiplies that by between tenfold and seven hundredfold, up to many multiples. The exegetes are agreed on His saying ﴿وَمَن جاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَلا يُجْزى إلا مِثْلَها﴾, because the evil deed here is associating partners with Allah; and they said: "whoever comes with the good deed" — it is saying "There is no god but Allah". The root of good deeds is the affirmation of oneness (tawḥīd), and the worst of evil deeds is disbelief in Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.

zajjaj:161-161.t:
﴿قُلْ إنَّنِي هَدانِي رَبِّي إلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾: ”اَلصِّراطُ“ is the religion; [i.e.] "who has directed me to the religion that is the religion of truth". Then He explained that and said: ﴿دِينًا قِيَمًا﴾; ”اَلْقِيَمُ“ is the upright. It has also been read ”دِينًا قَيِّمًا“. ”قِيَمٌ“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like ”اَلصِّغَرُ“ (smallness) and ”اَلْكِبَرُ“ (greatness), except that He did not say ”قِوَمٌ“, as in His saying ﴿لا يَبْغُونَ عَنْها حِوَلا﴾ [al-Kahf: 108], because your saying ”قامَ قِيَمًا“ is as though it were based on ”قَوُمَ“ or ”قَوِمَ“; when [the verb] became weak (iʿtalla) and became ”قامَ“, ”قِيَمٌ“ became weak too. As for ”حِوَلٌ“, it is on the basis that it runs on no verb.

As for the accusative of ﴿دِينًا قِيَمًا مِلَّةَ إبْراهِيمَ حَنِيفًا﴾, it is construed by meaning, because when He said ﴿هَدانِي رَبِّي إلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾, that indicated "He made known to me an upright religion" (”عَرَّفَنِي دِينًا قِيمًا“). And it is possible that it is a badal (substitute) from the meaning of "He guided me to a straight path"; the meaning: "He guided me [on] a straight path, an upright religion", as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَيَهْدِيَكَ صِراطًا مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 2]. ”مِلَّةَ إبْراهِيمَ“ is a badal from ”دِينًا قِيَمًا“, and ”حَنِيفًا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ”إبْراهِيمَ“; the meaning is: "He guided me and made known to me the creed of Ibrāhīm in the state of his being ḥanīf". Here it is better [taken] for Ibrāhīm than for another. ﴿وَما كانَ مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ﴾. We have already explained the meaning of ”اَلْحَنِيفِيَّةُ“: that it is inclining towards Islam with an inclination that has no turning back.

zajjaj:162-162.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ إنَّ صَلاتِي ونُسُكِي ومَحْيايَ ومَماتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾: they said: ”اَلنُّسُكُ“ is sacrificial slaughter, and ”اَلنُّسُكُ“ is whatever is offered to draw near to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He. ﴿وَمَحْيايَ ومَماتِي﴾: the yāʾ is the yāʾ of annexation (possessive yāʾ); it takes fatḥa because its origin is fatḥa, and it may be given sukūn when what precedes it is vowelled. ”مَماتِي“ is permissible: if you wish, you read ”مَماتِيَ لِلَّهِ“ with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and if you wish, you give it sukūn. As for the yāʾ of ”مَحْيايَ“, it must take fatḥa, because what precedes it is quiescent.

The meaning of the verse is that he informs that one draws near through prayer and all the rites only to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, not to other than Him, as the idolaters used to slaughter for their idols. So He made known that it is Allah alone, by His saying: ﴿لا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وبِذَلِكَ أُمِرْتُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 163].

zajjaj:164-164.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ أغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أبْغِي رَبًّا وهو رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾, that is: He originated all things; no one is able to originate anything of them.

And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى﴾, that is: no sinful soul is taken to account for the sin of another; no one is taken to account for another's wrongdoing.

zajjaj:165-165.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكم خَلائِفَ الأرْضِ﴾: it is said: "the successors of the earth" are the community of Muḥammad ﷺ, because the Prophet ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets, so his community has succeeded all the other communities. Some said: "successors of the earth" means some of you succeed others. ﴿وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكم فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجاتٍ لِيَبْلُوَكم في ما آتاكُمْ﴾: by this He indicated that He has favoured some people in order to test them in what He has provided them; and He, exalted is His praise, knows what will come from them before that, except that He tests them so that what reward and punishment are based on becomes manifest from them.

And His saying: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ العِقابِ وإنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾: if someone says: How is it said "swift in punishment", when His punishment is only on the Day of Resurrection, even though some of it has occurred in this world? That is only because the matter of the Hour is swift, since everything that passes away, even if it is long drawn out, is in the position of what is not perceived, for swiftness. Likewise His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿وَما أمْرُ السّاعَةِ إلا كَلَمْحِ البَصَرِ أوْ هو أقْرَبُ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 77], and likewise His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إنَّهم يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيدًا﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 6] ﴿وَنَراهُ قَرِيبًا﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 7].

zajjaj:73-73.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾: «يوم» is accusative on two aspects. One of them is on the meaning «واتقوه، ويوم يقول …» ("and fear Him, and the day He says …"), so that it is co-ordinated (nasaq) with the hāʾ [of «اتقوه»], as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿واتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 48]. The better is that it be on the meaning «واذكر يقول كن فيكون» ("and mention [the day] He says: Be, and it is"), because after it comes ﴿وَإذْ قالَ إبْراهِيمُ لأبِيهِ آزَرَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 74].
[Translator's note: «يوم» is missing from the printed paraphrase «واذكر يقول كن فيكون»; the sense requires «واذكر يومَ يقول».]
There is a third aspect in it, which is conjunction with ﴿السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ﴾, the meaning being: "and He it is who created the heavens and the earth in truth, and created the day He says: Be, and it is".

If someone says: "The Day of Resurrection has not yet come", [the answer is that] whatever Allah has informed us will come to be, its reality is occurring without doubt.

And His words: ﴿كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾: some said the address here is to the forms (al-ṣuwar), the meaning being "and the day He says to the forms: Be, and it is", and the mention made of «الصور» indicates it. It has also been said that His word «كن» contains the names of all that is created at that time, the meaning being "and the day He says to the thing: Be, and it is". This is mentioned to indicate the speed of the matter of the resurrection and the Hour, as if He said: "and the day He says to creation: Die, and they die; and Spread out, and they spread out" — as if He commands life and it comes to be in them, and death, and it descends first, [and] all creation perishes.

It has also been said: «ويوم يقول كن فيكون» — ﴿قَوْلُهُ﴾, i.e. "He commands, and His command takes place", and ﴿الحَقُّ﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوله», just as you say «قد قلتَ فكان قولُك» ("you said, and your word came to be"): the meaning is not that you spoke and the speech came to be; the meaning is only that what the speech indicated came to be. On the first view, «قوله» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الحق» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

And His words: ﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ﴾: the accusative of «يوم» may be on ﴿وَلَهُ المُلْكُ يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ﴾, explaining His words «ويوم يقول كن فيكون». It may also be accusative by «قوله الحق», the meaning being: "and His word is the truth on the day the trumpet is blown".

If someone says: "Dominion belongs to Allah at all times, so why are the Day of Resurrection and the day the trumpet is blown singled out?", the answer to this is that it is the day in which no benefit or harm from anyone to anyone appears, as He said: ﴿والأمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 19], while the command at every time belongs to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

They have two views on «الصور»: it is said in the exegesis that «الصور» is the name of a horn that is blown into; and it is said that «الصُّوَر» is the plural of «صورة» (form). Both are permissible, and the more firmly established of them in ḥadīth and transmission is that «الصور» is a horn; and «الصور» as the plural of «صورة» — the people of the language hold to this.

zajjaj:74-74.t: And His words: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ إبْراهِيمُ لأبِيهِ آزَرَ﴾: with the accusative (fatḥa) and with ḍamma. Whoever reads with ḍamma does so as a vocative (nidāʾ), the meaning being: "O Āzar, do you take idols?". There is no disagreement among the genealogists that the name of Ibrāhīm's father is "Tāriḥ", while what is in the Qurʾān indicates that his name is "Āzar".
